content.rendered:
We are looking for dynamic and motivated professionals for the following positions:

Posiiton: Finance & Accounts Officer
Unit: Jagdamba Construction Solutions Pvt. Ltd
Location: Naxal

Key Responsibilities:

  • Manage daily accounting, invoicing, payments, and bank reconciliation.
  • Prepare monthly financial statements, MIS, budgets, and variance reports.
  • Monitor receivables and coordinate with the Recovery Officer on collections.
  • Handle tax compliance, audits, and financial documentation.
  • Coordinate with branches, banks, auditors, OEMs, and internal teams.
  • Support management in financial planning, cost control, and customer financing.

Qualifications & Skills:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Management, or related field.
  • 2+ years of relevant experience.

Position: Regional Officer – 2W Sales (Premium Segment)

Unit: Jagdamba Motors Pvt. Ltd
Location: Western Area (HQ: Butwal)

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop and execute dealer/channel-wise sales plans to achieve assigned targets.
  • Monitor model-wise, dealer-wise retail and billing performance.
  • Manage enquiries and review showroom performance regularly.
  • Coordinate ATL/BTL marketing activities and trade promotions.
  • Monitor collections and minimize dealer outstanding dues.
  • Develop new dealers and ensure dealership standards and staff training.
  • Track competitor activities and prepare regular market reports.
  • Conduct dealer visits and monitor plan vs. achievement.

Qualifications & Skills:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Management or related field.
  • 2–4 years of experience in sales/dealership operations, preferably in automobiles.

Posiiton: BTL Account Officer
Unit: Jagdamba Motors Pvt. Ltd
Location: Naxal, Kathmandu

Key Responsibilities:

  • Prepare and manage sales budgets with Sales and Accounts teams.
  • Conduct budget planning, forecasting, and expense projections.
  • Monitor budget vs. actual expenses and analyze variances.
  • Track and control sales-related expenditures.
  • Verify and process dealer claims and supporting documents.
  • Coordinate budgets for exchange events and promotional activities.
  • Support PO creation with proper budget verification.

Qualifications & Skills:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Management, Finance, or a related field.
  • 2+ years of experience in sales budgeting, MIS, or financial reporting.
  • Strong analytical and advanced Excel skills.

Interested candidates can send their updated CV to: vacancy@jagdambamotors.com

Position: Training Coordinator
Location: Sanobharyang, Kathmandu

We are looking for a proactive and organized Service Training Coordinator to support service operations, manpower reporting, CSP development, and technical training coordination.

Key Responsibilities

  • Coordinate with RMs, SEs, dealers, and vendors for CSP establishment, standardization, branding, and documentation.
  • Prepare and maintain 2W & 3W manpower, CSP, variance, manpower loss, and service initiation reports.
  • Identify training needs and coordinate training programs with relevant teams.
  • Coordinate EV training for technicians and ensure effective participation.
  •  Prepare regular reports and presentations for management review.
  •  Maintain CSP agreements, records, and related documentation.
  •  Coordinate with vendors for CSP branding and painting and ensure timely completion.

What We’re Looking For

  • Strong coordination and communication skills.
  • Good reporting and documentation abilities.
  • Proficiency in MS Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Ability to coordinate with multiple stakeholders and manage deadlines.
  •  Experience in automobile/service operations or training coordination will be an advantage.

Apply Now: Send your CV to vacancy@jagdambamotors.com.

FAO’s commitment to environmental sustainability is integral to our strategic objectives and operations.

Organizational Setting

FAO is a specialized agency of the UN that leads international efforts to defeat hunger. FAO’s goal is to achieve food security for all and ensure that people have regular access to enough high-quality food to lead active, healthy lives. With 195 Members (194 countries and the European Union), FAO works in over 130 countries worldwide.

FAO Country Offices, working under overall corporate guidance and in line with the Strategic Framework, offer policy advice and support to countries in the mandated areas of FAO, facilitated through partnerships, resources and an active country programme to provide technical assistance, develop capacities and deliver core services while fully observing international standards of accountability to establish leadership and strengthen impact at the country level.

The offices deliver on the programmatic priorities of each country as agreed in their respective Country Programming Frameworks (CPFs) aligned to the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) and ensure effective and efficient operations with adequate human and financial resources.

Specifically, FAO Country Offices:

  • advocate, inform and support policies and investments in the areas of FAO’s mandate;
  • provide technical assistance and deliver core services;
  • assist and catalyse partnership and resource mobilization activities to support agrifood systems transformation;
  • Position FAO as the specialized/authoritative technical agency in food and agriculture and agrifood systems transformation;
  • ensure risk-smart and accountable operations and management.

The position is located in the Sudurpashchim Province, based in the Provincial office of the FAO Nepal Country Office, and will support the field implementation of projects in the region. The Provincial Coordinator for Sudurpaschim Province will serve as the primary focal point for the project at the provincial level, ensuring effective planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of project activities in close collaboration with provincial and local government authorities, implementing partners, community stakeholders, and FAO Nepal. The incumbent will facilitate stakeholder engagement, strengthen partnerships, support work plan development and execution, monitor progress against agreed targets, identify and address implementation bottlenecks, ensure compliance with project requirements and donor obligations, organize meetings and capacity development activities, and contribute to knowledge management, documentation, and reporting. The Provincial Coordinator will also provide strategic and technical support to promote alignment of project interventions with provincial priorities, enhance local ownership, and ensure the timely achievement of project outcomes and sustainable impact across Sudurpaschim Province.

Reporting Lines

The Provincial Coordinator works under the overall supervision of the FAOR in Nepal, direct supervision of the Assistant FAOR (Programme), and in close coordination with the Emergency and Resilience Coordinator, and the technical supervision of the FAORAP/HQs, and in close consultation and coordination with the government counterparts.

Technical Focus

The Provincial Coordinator will support provincial-level planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring and reporting of FAO projects in Sudurpashchim Province and the western region of Lumbini Province, with emphasis on stakeholder coordination, capacity development, quality assurance, climate resilience, gender equality and social inclusion, and timely achievement of project results.

Tasks and responsibilities

  • Coordinate provincial-level planning and implementation of ReFAME activities in line with the project document and approved annual work plans, ensuring disaggregated planning by year, district, and budget headings.
  • Support the Project Management Unit (PMU) in effective execution of project activities, including finalization of Letters of Agreement (LOA)/contracts in consultation with the PMU, and maintain close coordination with the FAO Nepal Country Office.
  •  Conduct regular field monitoring visits to track progress, address implementation bottlenecks, and ensure quality and timely delivery.
  • Coordinate and maintain strong working relationships with the PMU, Ministry of Industry, Tourism, Forest and Environment (Sudurpashchim Province), Division Forest Offices, Provincial Ministries, Local Governments, UN agencies, INGOs, NGOs, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure harmonized, complementary, and sustainable interventions.
  •  Lead and support capacity-building initiatives, including capacitating human resources hired by the Operational Partner (OP), government counterparts, community institutions, and project beneficiaries for smooth implementation.
  •  Develop concept notes and detailed budget estimates for project activities and events, integrating gender equality, social inclusion, and climate resilience considerations.
  •  Support and monitor implementation of related FAO projects in Sudurpashchim and western region of Lumbini Province (e.g., ReFAME, GAFSP-PO, Four Better Model Village) to ensure quality of implementation, synergy and complementarities.
  • Facilitate visits from FAO CO, RAP, HQ, government counterparts, and other stakeholders, and coordinate with technical officers for necessary support.
  •  Represent FAO Nepal at provincial and local coordination meetings, workshops, and technical forums, including emergency-response, food security and nutrition coordination mechanisms and line agencies.
  •  Apply accountability and quality assurance mechanisms, organize periodic review and reflection meetings, coordinate Project Task Force meetings, and prepare required progress reports (quarterly, biannual, annual) in line with project, OPA, and donor requirements, documenting lessons learned and good practices.
  •  Provide coordination support to short-term consultants and undertake additional technical, coordination, or operational assignments (e.g., ITB, RFQ, RFP, BOQ, M&E, reporting, proposal development, etc.) as requested by the FAO Country Office to ensure effective achievement of project results.

CANDIDATES WILL BE ASSESSED AGAINST THE FOLLOWING

Minimum Requirements

  • Master’s degree in agricultural science, international development, natural resource management, climate change or any other related field.
  • At least five years of progressive professional experience in implementation, coordination and management of agriculture, agrifood systems, rural development, climate resilience, natural resource management or development programmes.
  •  Working knowledge of English (level C).
  •  National of Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal or resident of the country with a valid work permit.

FAO Core Competencies

  •  Results Focus
  • Teamwork
  • Communication
  • Building Effective Relationships
  •  Knowledge Sharing and Continuous Improvement

Technical/Functional Skills

  •  Work experience in more than one location or area of work, particularly in field-based assignments.
  • Extent and relevance of experience in coordinating agriculture, agrifood systems, rural development, climate resilience or natural resource management projects.
  •  Demonstrated experience working with provincial and local governments, civil society organizations, UN agencies, development partners and other stakeholders.
  •  Experience in project planning, monitoring, reporting, budgeting, capacity development and coordination of service providers or operational partners.

Selection Criteria

  •  Strong experience in provincial-level coordination, field implementation and stakeholder engagement.
  • Proven ability to prepare and monitor work plans, budgets, procurement-related inputs, risk registers and progress reports.
  •  Demonstrated capacity to organize and facilitate training, workshops, review meetings and technical coordination forums.
  • Strong skills in monitoring implementation, documenting results, preparing reports and addressing operational bottlenecks.
  •  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work collaboratively and deliver results under pressure

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

  • FAO does not charge a fee at any stage of the recruitment process (application, interview meeting, processing)
  • Applications received after the closing date will not be accepted
  • Please note that FAO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU) / United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). The list can be accessed at http://www.whed.net/
  • For additional employment opportunities visit the FAO employment website: http://www.fao.org/employment/home/en/
  • Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, and security clearances.

FAO seeks gender, geographical and linguistic diversity in its staff and international consultants in order to best serve FAO Members in all regions.

HOW TO APPLY

  • To apply, visit the recruitment website at Jobs at FAO and complete your online profile. We strongly recommend that your profile is accurate, complete and includes your employment records, academic qualifications, and language skills
  • Candidates are requested to attach a letter of motivation to the online profile
  • Once your profile is completed, please apply, and submit your application
  •  Please note that FAO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU) / United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). The list can be accessed at http://www.whed.net/. These qualifications should be in alignment with the International Standard Classification of Education (ISCED) mappings.
  •  Candidates may be requested to provide performance assessments and authorization to conduct verification checks of past and present work, character, education, military and police records to ascertain any and all information which may be pertinent to the employment qualifications
  •  Incomplete applications will not be considered
  • Personal information provided on your application may be shared within FAO and with other companies acting on FAO’s behalf to provide employment support services such as pre-screening of applications, assessment tests, background checks and other related services. You
  • will be asked to provide your consent before submitting your application. You may withdraw consent at any time, by withdrawing your application, in such case FAO will no longer be able to consider your application
  • Only applications received through the FAO recruitment portal will be considered
  • Your application will be screened based on the information provided in your online profile
  • We encourage applicants to submit the application well before the deadline date.

If you need help or have queries, please create a one-time registration with FAO’s client support team for further assistance: https://fao.service-now.com/csp

The National Federation of the Disabled Nepal (NFDN) is a national umbrella organization of persons with disabilities and has been consistently working to promote and protect the rights of persons with disabilities in Nepal since 1993. NFDN is seeking a highly qualified, experienced and motivated professionals for the position of Project Coordinator to implement Include Us phase II project supported by CBM Global Nepal.

Interested candidates are requested to visit the NFDN website, www.nfdn.org.np review the detailed Terms of Reference/Job Description and required qualifications and submit their application along with the following documents:

  •  An updated CV;
  •  A cover letter mentioning the expected salary; and
  •  Contact details, including telephone number and email address of two referees.

The interested candidates are requested to apply from the online link: https://ee.kobotoolbox.org/x/QcKDFIvF no later than October 17, 2026.

NFDN reserves the right to cancel, postpone, modify or withdraw the recruitment process, and to reject any application without assigning any reason.

Candidates applying for these positions must comply with NFDN’s policies, guidelines, and code of conduct, including its Safeguarding, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH), and Anti-Corruption policies, as well as all associated standards and procedures.

1. Project Coordinator- NFDN Federal Office Kathmandu

Job purpose:

The Project Coordinator (PC) is responsible for overseeing the overall project cycle management of the Include Us Phase II Project and related NFDN programmes, ensuring effective, timely, inclusive and quality implementation in line with NFDN’s principles, policies, strategic priorities and agreed project standards. The PC will provide technical and strategic support to project and provincial staff, coordinate with OPDs, government authorities, partners, donors and other stakeholders and oversee programme planning, advocacy, capacity building, awareness raising, networking, budget management, communication, reporting, monitoring and evaluation. The PC will serve as NFDN’s focal point for federal and provincial project coordination, promote the meaningful participation of persons with all types of disabilities, support project and resource development and ensure that good practices, evidence and lessons learned are documented and applied to strengthen NFDN’s programmes.

Major Responsibilities

1. Project Planning, Implementation and Quality Assurance

  • Lead the planning, implementation, monitoring and quality assurance of project activities in accordance with the approved project design, agreement, workplan, budget, indicators, NFDN strategy and roadmap.
  •  Develop appropriate implementation modalities, processes, tools and workplans and ensure that activities are implemented effectively, on time and within the approved budget.
  • Ensure timely planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, review and reporting of project activities, with appropriate quality assurance throughout the project cycle.
  •  Ensure that project approaches and interventions are responsive to the needs and priorities of persons with disabilities and comply with NFDN, partner and donor policies, procedures and standards.
  •  Monitor project progress against agreed outputs, results, deliverables and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), and take or recommend corrective measures where necessary.
  •  Contribute to the achievement of monthly and quarterly project operational and quality targets.
  •  Ensure meaningful participation of persons with disabilities and OPDs representing different impairment groups in project planning, implementation, monitoring and review.

2. Provincial and Local-Level Coordination

  • Monitor the implementation of project activities by provincial offices and provide technical guidance, mentoring, recommendations and corrective support to Province Managers, Province Advocacy Officers and other relevant staff.
  • Provide technical support and guidance for project activities at provincial, district and municipal levels.
  •  Coordinate with OPDs in project-targeted provinces and municipalities to facilitate their meaningful engagement in advocacy, policy dialogue, access to justice, accessibility and other project initiatives.
  •  Coordinate with federal, provincial and local government authorities, OPDs, rights holders, civil society organizations and other relevant stakeholders to facilitate effective project implementation.
  • Explore and strengthen networking and collaboration opportunities at federal, provincial and local levels relevant to the project.

3. Advocacy, Disability Rights and Capacity Building

  • Promote and support a human rights-based and disability-inclusive approach in all project activities, consistent with the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD), national legislation and relevant international standards.
  • Support OPDs and persons with disabilities to advocate for their rights, access to justice, accessibility and inclusive policies and programmes.
  • Contribute to the development of advocacy strategies for consideration by the NFDN Board to influence relevant federal, provincial and local authorities in strengthening disability-inclusive policies, programmes and services.
  •  Identify capacity-building needs and facilitate training, orientation, coaching and mentoring for project staff, OPDs, persons with disabilities and other relevant stakeholders in coordination with the Administrative Manager and General Secretary.
  • Support NFDN Board members in project-related advocacy campaigns, awareness-raising, capacity-building, networking and collaboration activities.

4. Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning

  • Develop and maintain appropriate tools and formats for collecting, analysing and documenting project data from national, provincial, district, municipal and OPD levels.
  •  Ensure systematic monitoring of project progress, results, achievements, challenges, lessons learned and good practices.
  •  Conduct or facilitate quarterly internal reviews covering programme, operational and financial performance, and provide constructive feedback and recommendations for improvement.
  • Prepare monthly, periodic narrative and other reports required by NFDN, project partners and donors in accordance with agreed reporting requirements.
  • Ensure that reports accurately capture relevant data, progress, results, achievements, challenges, case studies, lessons learned and good practices.
  • Prepare and document case studies, success stories and other evidence of project results and impact.
  • Ensure that project information, relevant national and international legal frameworks, policies, guidelines, research and other useful resources are compiled and shared with NFDN member organizations through accessible communication channels, including email, telephone, website, social media, publications, meetings and orientations.

5. Coordination, Communication and Project Governance

  • Facilitate effective communication and coordination among the project team, NFDN management, Board members, provincial offices, OPDs, partners and other stakeholders.
  • Ensure that project staff, Board members and key stakeholders have a clear understanding of project objectives, expected results, roles and responsibilities, and provide leadership and motivation to achieve agreed goals.
  • Organize and facilitate meetings of project partners, the Project Steering Committee and other project structures in accordance with the approved implementation plan.
  • Prepare agendas, minutes, action points and other necessary documentation and ensure timely follow-up on agreed decisions.
  • Provide regular and timely information to the Administrative Manager and General Secretary on project progress, implementation issues, risks, opportunities, financial and operational matters, and required management decisions.
  • Liaise, in coordination with the Line Manager, with the International Office, I/NGOs, project partners, consultants, advisors, NFDN Board members, Province Managers and other stakeholders connected with the project.

6. Risk Management and Technical Quality

  •  Ensure that appropriate technical quality standards are maintained throughout project implementation.
  •  Identify, document and analyse technical, operational and implementation risks and opportunities and recommend appropriate mitigation or improvement measures.
  •  Collect and analyse relevant technical information and ensure that evidence and lessons learned inform project planning and implementation.
  •  Ensure compliance with NFDN, partner and donor requirements and established project procedures.

7. Project Development and Resource Mobilization

  •  Identify emerging needs, opportunities and innovative approaches for the development of new projects and programmes aligned with NFDN’s strategic priorities.
  •  Support the Administrative Manager and General Secretary in donor mapping, resource mobilization, proposal development and submission to potential partners and donors.
  •  Develop concise concept notes or one-page activity papers for planned activities based on the approved project plan before implementation and facilitate the required internal approval process.
  • Document and promote innovative practices, lessons learned and evidence that can contribute to future programme development.

8. Overall Accountability

  •  Ensure that project activities are implemented efficiently, effectively and transparently, with appropriate accountability for time, budget, quality and results.
  •  Perform other project-related duties and responsibilities assigned by the General Secretary, Administrative Manager or other authorized NFDN authority in accordance with NFDN policies and procedures.
  • Regular implementation and follow up of the programs and also follow the recommendations arising from the reviews, audits, monitoring visits and internal and donor assessment
  • Be responsible for ensuring the expenditure follows approved budgets, approvals, donor and organisational policies, documentation requirements.

Qualification, experiences and skills requirements:

  • Master degree in social work, development studies, education, management, law or related field (disability study is preferred).
  • Minimum of five years of experience in I/NGO environment, including experience coordinating and implementing programs. besides project management experience, specifically require demonstrated experience with the donor compliance, budget monitoring, internal controls and procurement procedures.
  •  Experience in social sector with a proven experience of working with persons with disabilities/OPD. (Experience on disability inclusion related project or advocacy is preferred).
  •  Good skills of the risk identification and prompt response to the risks as stated in the risk register
  •  Good knowledge and understanding of UNCRPD and national law related to disability.
  •  Good understanding of disability context / concerns and rights
  •  Good experience in disability inclusion and accessibility with leadership quality to coordinate and influence the governments bodies.
  •  Good experience of working with different impairment groups/OPDs at province & municipal level.
  •  Strong communication, documentation, coordination and team-building skills.
  •  Excellent written and verbal communication in Nepali and English
  •  Good computer skill in operating basic computer programs such as MS office packs with email and internet handling
  • Skillful in searching information in internet, operating social media, making news, activity, and periodic reports when needed.

    NFDN follows the organization policies and guidelines including safeguarding and anti-corruption policies and ensure compliance to all aspects of the Safeguarding and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, abuse and harassment policies and associated standards and procedures. NFDN is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified women and person with disability are strongly encouraged to apply. NFDN always encourage the inclusion and integration of people with disabilities and female candidate in its program and plans.

Organizational Setting

FAO is a specialized agency of the UN that leads international efforts to defeat hunger. FAO’s goal is to achieve food security for all and ensure that people have regular access to enough high-quality food to lead active, healthy lives. With 195 Members (194 countries and the European Union), FAO works in over 130 countries worldwide.

FAO Country Offices, working under overall corporate guidance and in line with the Strategic Framework, offer policy advice and support to countries in the mandated areas of FAO, facilitated through partnerships, resources and an active country programme to provide technical assistance, develop capacities and deliver core services while fully observing international standards of accountability to establish leadership and strengthen impact at the country level.

The offices deliver on the programmatic priorities of each country as agreed in their respective Country Programming Frameworks (CPFs) aligned to the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) and ensure effective and efficient operations with adequate human and financial resources.

Specifically, FAO Country Offices:

  • advocate, inform and support policies and investments in the areas of FAO’s mandate;

Reporting Lines

The Programme Assistant will work under the overall supervision of the FAO Representative and direct supervision of the Assistant FAO Representative (Programme) in close consultation with programme cluster team.

Technical Focus

The Programme Assistant provides technical and operational support for project implementation by preparing programme documents and reports, compiling and analysing data from corporate systems, and ensuring accurate documentation and filing. The role supports monitoring activities, organizes meetings and missions, manages correspondence, and assists in producing background materials. It also contributes to project coordination, logistical arrangements, and routine administrative tasks to ensure smooth delivery of programme operations.

Tasks and responsibilities

The Programme Assistant will be responsible to carry out the following tasks:

  • Assist in the preparation of project proposals/documents, project briefs, project progress/final reports, background papers, sections of reports and studies.
  •  Collect and compile data on programme/project activities to support reporting on programme/ project delivery.
  •  Process, format and proof-read reports, documents, publications, and correspondence related to the work of the Country office from draft texts.
  •  Review and direct correspondence, calls and queries to appropriate contacts; provide for background information; respond to routine enquiries.
  •  Assist in the organization of policy dialogues, workshops and consultation meetings and preparation for project periodic reviews, field monitoring and supervision missions in close consultation with programme team, government counterparts and other relevant stakeholders.
  •  Make arrangements for meetings, seminars and events: implement logistics, prepare meeting minutes, correspondences, compile and distribute documents, support in administrative arrangements.
  •  Enter, select, analyse, and summarize data from various sources, including FAO corporate systems, such as COIN (Country Office Information System), FPMIS (Field Programme Management Information System), Global Resource Management System (GRMS), country databases, etc to support programme operations.
  •  Maintain log, file and update records in prescribed format for subsequent use.
  •  Participate in project monitoring by maintaining current registers and controlling tools on the status of projects at various stages; review inputs, expenditures, and time frames according to work plans; make necessary abstracts and computations; detect inconsistencies.
  •  Assist in the preparation and submission of periodic and ad hoc project and country office reports.
  •  Prepare background material, working papers and tables for briefings, review sessions and meetings.
  •  Prepare correspondence to verify data, answer queries, and obtain additional information on transactions and operational matters, as required.
  •  Maintain a filing system of technical and project documents and correspondence.
  •  Carry out other specific operational tasks for programme/ project implementation as requested.
  • Perform other related duties as required.

  •  Teamwork
  •  Communication
  • Building Effective Relationships
  •  Knowledge Sharing and Continuous Improvement

Technical/Functional Skills

  •  Ability to draft, format and proof‑read programme documents and reports.
  •  Skills in data collection, entry and basic analysis using corporate systems.
  •  Experience supporting meetings, workshops and field missions.
  •  Strong administrative skills, including filing, record‑keeping and monitoring tools.

Transcultural Psychosocial Organization Nepal (TPO Nepal) is one of Nepal’s leading organizations in psychosocial and mental health support. It was established in 2005 with the aim of promoting psychosocial well-being and mental health of people in need through the development of sustainable, culturally-appropriate and community-based mental health and psychosocial support systems.

TPO Nepal is implementing a project named “Mental Health and Psycho-social Support interventions to Individuals, Families and Communities affected by the Flash Flood” funded by Americares Foundation, which aims to improve the mental health, psychosocial well-being, functioning and resilience of individuals, families and communities affected by the flash flood through evidence based MHPSS interventions and strengthened community and health system support.

In this regard, TPO Nepal is looking for a competent, committed and result-oriented candidate for the following position.

  • Conduct regular field visits to project-implemented areas.

NIDWAN is a national non-profit organization led by Indigenous women with disabilities, working to promote dignity, equality, and social justice for Indigenous women and girls with disabilities across Nepal. NIDWAN’s vision is a just, inclusive, and equitable society where Indigenous women including underrepresented groups with disabilities, fully enjoy their human rights and actively participate in all spheres of life. Its mission is to empower Indigenous and underrepresented groups with disabilities through advocacy, leadership development, access to inclusive services (including health and SRH), and strengthened institutional and community systems that uphold their rights. NIDWAN is guided by core values and principles of human rights, gender equality, disability inclusion, Indigenous peoples’ rights, participation and leadership of persons with disabilities with an intersectional approach, accountability, and partnership. NIDWAN has been working collaboratively with Government, UN agencies like WFP, UNDP, UN Women, civil society, and development partners to ensure that no one is left behind. In addition, NIDWAN has done movement building with feminist, disability, indigenous and youth movements. From its decade-long experiences, NIDWAN is equipped with competencies regarding gender-responsive and disability inclusive education, climate, health care systems, and health-related social services.

Position: Finance Coordinator

End Date: October 8, 2026

With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type: Local – Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

This position is responsible for performing financial accounting, account reconciliation, and review of expenses, including the processing and review of journal entries and vouchers in the financial system. The position will also support the preparation of accounting records and financial statements and oversee accounts payable and receivable activities in compliance with WVI financial policies, standards, and applicable statutory requirements.

The position will be responsible for ensuring the effective and efficient utilization and management of organizational financial resources through strong financial controls, timely and accurate reporting, compliance, and continuous improvement of financial systems and processes, ultimately contributing to better stewardship of resources for the benefit of children and communities.

In addition, the position will oversee the overall financial management, compliance, reporting, and control requirements related to US Government-funded activities and the Flood Response Project, ensuring adherence to applicable donor regulations, WVI policies and procedures, grant requirements, and statutory obligations. The position will coordinate closely with relevant Finance, Programme, Operations, and partner teams to ensure proper financial planning, monitoring, documentation, and accountability throughout the project lifecycle.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Financial Management and Multi-Donor Response Funding administration

  • Manage financial operations of Response Funding in accordance with diverse donor regulations, organizational policies, and approved budgets.
  • Maintain clear segment accounting to track, allocate, and monitor contributions coming from different funding organizations, ensuring no co-mingling of restricted funds.
  • Monitor project expenditures across all funding streams to ensure costs are allowable, allocable, reasonable, and properly documented according to specific donor agreements.
  • Review transactions and supporting documents for compliance with various donor requirements and organizational guidelines.
  • Monitor budget utilization across multiple donor accounts and provide regular analysis on spending trends, burn rates, and potential funding gaps.
  • Support project teams in multi-donor budget planning, budget revisions, co-funding allocations, and financial forecasting.
  • Ensure sufficient fund availability and proper donor account coding prior to processing response-related payments.

Financial Reporting

  • Prepare accurate and timely monthly, quarterly, annual, and donor-specific financial reports for management, institutional grants, and other funding sources in compliance with donor and Support Office (SO) templates.
  • Review General Ledger transactions to ensure proper expense coding and allocation across multiple funding streams.
  • Conduct regular account reconciliations, including bank accounts, advances, receivables, grant balances, cash receipts, and commitments against SO agreements.
  • Track matched funding and co-financing requirements between institutional grants and complementary funding sources.
  • Prepare financial analyses, variance reports, and pipeline updates for project management, grant closeout activities, and donor/SO review meetings.
  • Consolidate multi-donor financial data and resolve reporting queries from Support Offices, National Offices, and donor representatives.

Compliance and Internal Controls

  • Ensure compliance with terms, conditions, and regulations governing all contributing donor organizations, as well as organizational policies.
  • Maintain adequate supporting documentation, donor mapping records, and grant files for internal and external audit purposes.
  • Conduct periodic financial compliance reviews to manage risks associated with multi-donor funding rules and restrictions.
  • Support internal audits, external audits, donor-specific audits, and monitoring visits from funding partners.
  • Implement corrective action plans for audit findings and donor compliance recommendations.

Partner Financial Monitoring

  • Review partner financial reports, supporting documents, and fund utilization to ensure accuracy, completeness, and compliance.
  • Conduct periodic financial monitoring visits and desk reviews of implementing partners.
  • Monitor partner budget performance and expenditure trends against approved budgets.
  • Verify that partner transactions comply with donor regulations, grant agreements, and organizational policies.
  • Follow up on audit findings, monitoring recommendations, and corrective action plans.
  • Provide financial management guidance, coaching, and capacity-building support to partner finance and program staff.
  • Assess partner financial risks and recommend mitigation measures.
  • Ensure timely submission and review of partner financial reports and liquidation documents.
  • Support partner financial assessments, audits, and donor monitoring visits.
  • Maintain proper documentation of partner monitoring activities and compliance records.

Capacity Building, Technical Support & stakeholders Management

  • Provide financial guidance to project managers, budget holders, and partner organizations on managing multi-sourced response budgets.
  • Conduct training sessions on diverse donor requirements, multi-donor fund tracking, and compliance procedures.
  • Support partner organizations in strengthening their financial management and multi-fund accounting systems.
  • Serve as the primary technical resource person for Response Funding financial requirements.
  • Coordinate closely with program, procurement, logistics, and grant acquisition teams to align expenditure with funding organization commitments.
  • Liaise with funding organization representatives, auditors, banking institutions, and government agencies on financial matters.
  • Maintain strong working relationships with internal teams and external donor representatives.

KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE

Required Education, training, license, registration and certification

  • Bachelor Degree of Commerce, Business Studies or Equivalent
  • CIMA, CFA, ACCA, CA, CPA, preferred

Required Professional Experience

  • Minimum 3–5 years of progressive experience in finance, accounting, or grant financial management within an NGO, INGO, or donor-funded environment.
  • Proven experience in grant budgeting, financial reporting, fund management, and donor compliance.
  • At least 2–3 years of direct experience managing or supporting US Government-funded grants (e.g., USAID, USDA, BHA, CDC, Department of State, or other federal awards).
  • Experience in reviewing financial transactions to ensure allowability, allocability, reasonableness, and compliance with donor requirements.
  • Demonstrated experience in partner financial monitoring, capacity building, and financial risk assessment.
  • Experience in preparing and reviewing donor financial reports, budget forecasts, and grant reconciliations.
  • Experience supporting internal audits, external audits, donor reviews, and compliance assessments.
  • Strong understanding of internal controls, financial management systems, and accounting principles.
  • Experience working with ERP/accounting systems and advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and financial reporting tools.
  • Good interpersonal, problem solving & time management skills
  • Willingness to work under pressure with tight deadlines and to travel across the project areas.
  • Experience of working in a computerized accounting environment. (Sun Systems, Vision XL & Executive, others)

Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications

  • General Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP)
  • Excellent computer literacy & skill of MS office applications (Word/Excel/PowerPoint/internet etc.)
  • Good command of English & Nepali languages (written & spoken)
  • Practical knowledge of project budgeting, accounting & reporting
  • Able to articulate and communicate ideas well verbally and in writing
  • Understanding of World Vision Financial System & procedures

Position: Project Coordinator- Education
End Date: October 8, 2026

With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Job Description:

World Vision International Nepal (WVI Nepal) has launched a Category II Emergency Response in the districts of Rasuwa and Nuwakot, Bagmati Province, following devastating flash floods along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors that caused casualties, displacement and extensive damage across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. The 12-month Nepal Flash Flood Response (NFFR) 2026 plan which is funded by several donors targets 25,000 people, including 10,000 children, from around 5,000 affected households across seven sectors, moving from relief into early recovery. Thus, this position will be responsible for ensuring all education activities planned in World Vision’s Nepal Flash Flood Response Project are implemented and set education outcomes are achieved. The incumbent will work closely together with World Vision and partner NGO staff, as well as with the education department government staff. The educational response interventions take place particularly in Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts.

The incumbent captures key learning, integration related evidence and key outcomes of the given scope in the form of report, data management and other relevant communication materials. This role expects to take lead on education related matters and empowers teams to demonstrate in all plans and reports. A good team player and able to embrace change and adapt to changing context shaping plans and team cohesion is envisioned from this. This role envisions , managing issues and problem solving, innovative and agile leadership.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Project Implementation and Quality Assurance

  • Provide overall technical leadership to the World Vision team and partner NGOs implementing educational response interventions under the overall response plan.
  • Coordinate and mobilize the teams effectively to deliver quality results timely and effectively with safety measures in place.
  • Coordinate and mobilize the WV and partner NGO teams to deliver quality results timely and effectively, such as the establishment of temporary learning centers and/or emergency education activities in flood-affected areas, prioritizing locations with high risks of education discontinuity and school dropout.
  • Ensure that Psychosocial Support (PSS) to the flood-affected children is part of the emergency education activities.
  • Ensure WVI Global Center guidance, Education in Emergencies approaches, and government education policies are adhered to implement education-related activities as per the emergency response plan.
  • Support and capacitate the partner NGOs to implement the education response activities that include planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, and reporting in line with response plan.
  • Support in establishing a good working culture and team cohesion to implement and integrate education related interventions.
  • Ensure budget expenditure throughout the project cycle is as planned.
  • Conduct rapid education in emergencies assessments in flood affected communities, focusing on children, women, girls, children and persons with disabilities, Dalits, and indigenous groups and marginalized communities.
  • Ensure timely and quality implementation of education response interventions, including TLCs set up and its functionalization, creating a safe and stimulating home learning environment, conducting accelerated learning sessions and so on.
  • Ensure disaggregated data collection (sex, age, disability, caste/ethnicity) to inform inclusive programming.
  • Work closely with Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPD) to ensure the targeted people and children participate in the projects.
  • Conduct regular program reviews with partners to assess progress, address bottlenecks, and strengthen implementation quality.
  • Look out for possible risks and apply mitigation measures as necessary.
  • Lead project start-up, transition, close-out, and sustainability planning processes together with partners.
  • Facilitate integration of Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) principles throughout project planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation.

Monitoring, Information Management, and Learning

  • Conduct regular field monitoring visits to assess programme quality, effectiveness, compliance, and beneficiary satisfaction.
  • Monitor project performance against approved indicators, benchmarks, work plans, and donor commitments.
  • Verify program data through spot checks, field observations, and review of partner reporting systems.
  • Lead in providing technical guidance and support to use digital or other platforms to acquire data and information in the system.
  • Maintain proper and up to date assessment, monitoring and record keeping system to reflect in the MEAL and information management system.
  • Incorporate and address the relevant community feedback received wherever possible.
  • Capture all the key learning and successes for the case studies and publications to be shared with national and global arena.

Coordination, Collaboration & Representation

  • Coordinate with potential education stakeholders particularly at district and province level including government clusters, donors, UN agencies, and lNGOs .
  • Ensure representation at the districts and local education cluster meetings and provide real time updates and plans with them.
  • Provide regular updates to WVI Nepal national office inclusive education technical head regarding national level cluster meetings.
  • Ensure close coordination and collaboration with other functions within WVI Nepal including program, finance, public engagement, supply chain and sponsorship to ensure activities are carried out timely and efficiently.
  • Contribute to increased visibility, communication efforts and donor engagement by showcasing program achievements, impact, and learning.
  • Ensure 5W/ 3W reporting in Education Clusters and other government reporting requirements regularly.

Risk Management & Compliance

  • Identify, assess, and monitor program risks related to education in emergency, operational challenges, supply chains, and service delivery.
  • Develop and implement risk mitigation and contingency plans related to education programming in collaboration with partner NGOs, local authorities, and relevant stakeholders.
  • Ensure compliance with World Vision International policies, donor regulations, government guidelines, and humanitarian principles through engagement with partner NGOs and project visits.
  • Support partners in maintaining adequate documentation and evidence required for audits, donor reviews, and compliance assessments.
  • Strengthen accountability, transparency, safeguarding, and ethical practices throughout program implementation.
  • Abide by humanitarian principles and WV principles.

KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE

Required Education, training, license, registration and certification

  • Master’s degree in Education or Bachelor’s degree in Education with additional years of work experience

Required Professional Experience

  • At least 2 years (for those with Master degree) or 3-5 years (for Bachelor) working in the field of education as a sector
  • Knowledge of development and humanitarian sector

Essential Knowledge and Qualifications

  • Writing quality reports
  • Demonstrate collaboration & team building skills
  • Effective relationship management skills; ability to influence without having authority
  • Data management
  • Strong oral and written English and Nepali communication skills

Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications

  • Experience working in Education in Emergency context
  • Understand WV’s vision, core values and strategic mandates

Work Base: Nuwakot District

Duration: One year

Travel and/or Work Environment

Extensive travel to Rasuwa and Nuwakot of up to 60% of working time. Field travel may involve difficult road conditions, disrupted access, remote locations and basic accommodation.

Physical Requirements

Willingness and physical ability to travel to Rasuwa and Nuwakot, including remote and disaster-affected locations, for up to 60% of working time.

Excellent written and spoken English and Nepali.

With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Employee Contract Type:

Local – Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

The Response Supply Chain & Administration Coordinator is responsible for leading and coordinating all supply chain, procurement, logistics, fleet, warehouse, asset management and administration functions for the Nepal Flash Flood Response. The position ensures that all response operations are conducted in compliance with WVI policies, donor regulations, humanitarian principles, safeguarding requirements and Government of Nepal regulations while supporting efficient delivery of humanitarian and recovery interventions through both WVI Nepal and Partner NGO structures. The role works under the supervision of the Support Services Lead and collaborates closely with Operation teams, finance, security, MEAL, procurement vendors, and partner NGOs.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Supply Chain Operation and Coordination

  • Maintain strong functional alignment with WVI Nepal Supply Chain Department.
  • Ensure all procurement activities comply with WVI Nepal Supply Chain Policies, donor requirements and Delegation of Authority.
  • Collaborate with the National Office Supply Chain function on high-value, complex and strategic procurement activities.
  • Lead end-to-end procurement and supply chain operations for response and recovery activities.
  • Develop and monitor procurement plans aligned with project implementation schedules.
  • Participate in procurement committee meetings and supply chain review meetings.
  • Submit regular procurement, inventory, logistics and asset reports.
  • Escalate procurement risks, fraud concerns and compliance issues through appropriate channels.
  • Receive and review Purchase Requisitions and facilitate sourcing and procurement processes in accordance with policy.
  • Manage purchase orders, amendments and supplier coordination to ensure timely delivery of goods and services.
  • Coordinate closely with Partner NGOs to ensure timely procurement, logistics and supply chain support for project implementation.
  • Monitor procurement lead times and proactively address procurement bottlenecks affecting program delivery.
  • Track supply pipeline status and provide regular updates to the Support Services Lead and project teams.
  • Coordinate receipt, inspection, warehousing and dispatch of relief and recovery supplies.
  • Ensure accurate tracking of goods from procurement through distribution or final delivery.
  • Support emergency procurement and rapid response requirements during disaster response and recovery operations.
  • Coordinate with program, finance, MEAL and operations teams to ensure procurement activities support approved implementation plans and donor commitments.
  • Ensure procurement and logistics documentation is complete, properly filed and audit ready.

Administration, Assets and Fleet management

  • Manage general office administrative functions, including utilities, insurance, vehicle tax, renewal process, leave records, and inventory management.
  • Facilitate workshops, trainings, and events at the field office level, including logistics arrangement, coordination with hotels, catering service providers, and settlement of invoices.
  • Support documentation and filing systems, ensuring records are properly approved, stamped, and stored.
  • Ensure effective mobilization and scheduling of drivers based on field movement demands.
  • Maintain and review vehicle logbooks weekly, ensuring records include fuel, maintenance costs, and odometer readings
  • Ensure optimal fleet management in environmental safeguarding prospective (aging analysis, vehicle repair orders, track service quality) and calculate drivers’ overtime hours.
  • Oversee timely renewal of vehicle taxes and insurance.
  • Lead and execute the asset management policy and procedures in managing all the assets at field offices and with partner NGOs ensuring assets are updated on the Asset Management System, safeguarded, reconciled, and disposed of in a timely manner.
  • Ensure proper documentation and accountability for office and fleet-related expenditures.
  • Support the National Office in implementing the Global Insurance and REAM process in order to meet the global timelines.

Strategic Sourcing and Supplier Management

  • Develop and maintain consolidated procurement and sourcing plans in consultation with WVI response teams and Partner NGOs.
  • Conduct market assessments, supplier mapping, prequalification and price analysis to support informed sourcing decisions.
  • Lead RFQ/RFP processes, supplier negotiations and sourcing activities in accordance with WVI and donor requirements.
  • Facilitate procurement committee processes and ensure complete and compliant procurement documentation.
  • Provide oversight and technical support to Partner NGO procurement processes to ensure compliance with WVI policies and donor regulations.
  • Monitor procurement performance, supplier performance and procurement risks, and recommend corrective actions as required.
  • Coordinate with the National Supply Chain function to leverage framework agreements, approved supplier databases and strategic sourcing opportunities.
  • Support the preparation, review and administration of supplier contracts and service agreements in compliance with WVI and donor requirements.
  • Ensure suppliers understand agreed terms, delivery schedules, quality standards and contract requirements.
  • Monitor supplier performance and address contract or service delivery issues in a timely manner.
  • Coordinate contract renewals, amendments and close-out processes as required.
  • Maintain effective working relationships with suppliers to ensure uninterrupted support to response operations.
  • Ensure supplier contracts and procurement records are properly maintained and accessible for audit and compliance purposes.

Data Management, Analysis and Reporting

  • Monitor performance of key indicators, conduct root cause analysis of low performing areas and develop plans to improve those indicators
  • Conduct cost price analysis to formulate negotiation plans.
  • Analyze industry trends and market competitions to develop business improvement initiatives.

Compliance, Risk Management

  • Conduct regularly reviews of procurement policies, processes and guidelines to measure their effectiveness and applicability, including customer satisfaction and report to NO Management.
  • Advise National Offices on how to manage and maintain Logistics Tool & Dashboard for metric visibility in supply chain channels and timely communication with clients.
  • Review with Partners NGOs, their SCM Policies, procedures and etc. to identify any gaps, document them under assessment reports, and capture under capacity building plans.
  • Develop risk identification & assessment tools, registers and other tools and assess SCM related risks.
  • Develop proper filing and record keeping process for supply chain activities and ensure procurement audit trail is always available.
  • Monitor adherence to control measures and compliance with WV supply chain policies and guidelines.
  • Escalate any form of breach of controls, frauds, non-compliance, misappropriation of WV funds and assets related to SCM identified during the monitoring process.

Transcultural Psychosocial Organization Nepal (TPO) Nepal is one of Nepal’s leading psychosocial organizations. It was established in 2005 to promote psychosocial well-being and mental health of people in conflict-affected and other vulnerable communities through the development of sustainable, culturally-appropriate, and community-based psychosocial support systems.

Project information:

TPO Nepal is implementing activities under the “Strengthen systems for prevention and promotion of child and adolescent mental health” Flood Response project. The project aims to delivery safe, inclusive, ethical and quality mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) to children, adolescents, caregivers, families and other affected and vulnerable populations in communities affected by Bhotekoshi-Rasuwa Flash flood.

For this purpose, TPO Nepal seeks competent, committed and result oriented candidates for the following position:

Job Title : Psychiatrist/ MD

Job Station : Nuwakot

Number of Openings : 1 Full time

Job Duration : 6 Months (possibility to extension)

Start Date : At the earliest

Major responsibilities

The MD Psychiatrist will provide specialized clinical and technical leadership to the Community Mental Health Unit (CMHU) in flood-affected districts of Baghmati Province, Nepal, focusing on recovery and continuity of mental health services. The Psychiatrist will be responsible for following duties but not limited to:

  • Support the establishment and functioning of the CMHU and provide clinical supervision to the multidisciplinary team.
  • Conduct outreach clinics, providing psychiatric assessment, consultation, medication, follow-up and timely referral of complex and high-risk cases.
  • Maintain confidential clinical records and prepare required service and programme reports.Coordinate and support to psychologists, psychiatric nurses, counsellors and frontline health workers on case management and referral.
  • Facilitate mental health and psychosocial training, stress management, self-care sessions for frontline health workers.
  • Coordinate with municipalities, health facilities, government authorities and other stakeholders to strengthen community mental health services and referral mechanisms.
  • Ensure safeguarding, confidentiality, informed consent and child-friendly approaches in all service delivery.
  • Perform other relevant mental health services assigned by the organization.

Qualification, Skills and Experience:

  • MD in Psychiatry from a recognized university/institution.Valid registration with the Nepal Medical Council.
  • Relevant experience in providing psychiatric consultation, diagnosis, treatment, and referral services will be an advantage.
  • Experience in conducting mental health camps or providing mental health services in community settings will be preferred.
  • Good communication, interpersonal, documentation, and coordination skills.
  • Willingness to work in field settings and travel within the assigned area as required.
  • Commitment to confidentiality, professional ethics, safeguarding and respectful service delivery.

Interested, qualified, and motivated candidates meeting the above requirements are encouraged to apply along with a cover letter, updated resume (CV), and expected salary to: hrtponepal@tponepal.org.np. The last date for submitting the application is October 4, 2026.

Only short-listed candidates will be informed of the further selection process. Any activity intended to influence the selection process will lead to disqualification. All the selected candidates will undergo rigorous background checks.

TPO Nepal is committed to diversity and inclusion within its workforce. Individuals from minority groups, indigenous groups, and persons with disabilities are encouraged to apply. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence. TPO Nepal does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination.

The National Association of People Living with HIV in Nepal (NAP+N) is a national network established in 2003 and led by people living with HIV (PLHIV). It works in partnership with community-based organizations and local networks across Nepal to address the challenges of HIV and AIDS. NAP+N aims to strengthen community systems, ensure access to healthcare, and uphold the rights and dignity of PLHIV and key populations through advocacy, prevention, care, and support.

NAP+N is implementing the Community-Led Monitoring (CLM) initiative in 10 districts: Jhapa, Sunsari, Parsa, Dhanusha, Kathmandu, Chitwan, Kaski, Rupandehi, Kapilbastu and Kailali. This project aims to empower communities to monitor, evaluate, and improve HIV services through data-driven advocacy.

Detail of Job Title

No. of Positions: 1 (One)
Reports to: District Focal Person
Duty Station: Kathmandu
Salary & Benefits: As per the HR policy of NAP+N
 Contract Duration: Initially up to 31st December 2026 and possibilities of extension depending upon the performance

Roles and Responsibilities:

The CLM Leader will support the implementation of the Community-Led Monitoring (CLM) program at the district level. The role focuses on facilitating data collection from key and vulnerable populations affected by HIV, strengthening community participation, and supporting evidence-based advocacy for improved health services.

Key Responsibilities:

  •  Support implementation of CLM activities at community level.
  • Collect client feedback through tools such as Client Feedback Forms (CFF).
  • Support in facilitation of Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) and Key Informant Interviews (KIIs).
  •  Mobilize and engage key populations and community members.
  •  Coordinate with District Focal Person (DFP) and stakeholders.
  • Ensure proper documentation and timely reporting.
  • Assist in identifying service gaps and advocacy needs.
  • Maintain confidentiality and data quality.
  • Carry out other tasks as assigned by the District Focal Person (DFP) in support of the CLM objectives.

Required Qualifications and Competencies:

  • Minimum SLC/SEE with 2 years relevant experience in HIV field, OR
  • +2 (PCL) with at least 1 year relevant experience
  • Good understanding of PLHIV, key populations (KPs) and HIV-related issues.
  • Strong communication, facilitation, and coordination skills.
  • Ability to work in community settings and travel within the district.
  •  Experience with mobile-based data collection tools (preferred).
  •  Excellent interpersonal and coordination skills with stakeholders at various levels.

Organizational Context

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe. The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. The IFRC is currently present in Nepal through a Country Delegation (CD – first established in 1965 with a presence through regional representation at times), providing support to Nepal Red Cross Society (NRCS) programmes and National Society development (NSD) amongst as well as emergency response, other areas. The longer-term mission of the Nepal Delegation is to facilitate organisational growth, technical capacities, partnerships, and resource mobilisation that enable Nepal Red Cross Society to deliver on its humanitarian mandate in the country through the provision of technical support, advocacy, representation and coordination functions, in accordance with Strategy 2030, the IFRC Renewal and annual Operational Plans. The Country Delegation also provides integration services to six IFRC members with a presence in Nepal. On 26 August 2026, a major ice-rock avalanche occurred in the upper Bhote Koshi watershed near the China–Nepal border, resulting in an historically powerful flash flood that advanced from the border down the entire length of Nepal along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli River basins. This position is being hired to response to the operational requirements of the Flash Flood 2026 response operation, within a Federation-wide operation.

Job Purpose

To manage all IFRC fleet (all assets deployed in operation including IFRC and integrated PNS resources at a country level in-line with Global Fleet Policies & Procedures and Fleet Manual as well as other guidance, standards and processes to ensure a high-quality service provision that meets the needs of the Federation and service users with objectives of safety, environment and fleet management.

Job Duties and Responsibilities

  • Promote the Federation’s fleet management services and VRP to National Societies within the country including access to the VRP and purchasing services, Fleet Wave, end-of-life disposal, management, etc.
  • To be responsible that vehicle fleet is optimized in its size, vehicle models, utilization, running operational costs and is used as per set rules and regulations described in Fleet Manual.
  • To ensure timely, accurate and correct data entry into the fleet management system and to maintain vehicle fleet files with containing documentation with records of mileage, fuel, maintenance and repairs, accidents, and financial information as per Fleet Manual and set procedures.
  •  To plan, allocate and co-ordinate local driver resources to ensure the most effective use of their time and the efficient delivery of transport services using available resourcing and route planning tools as appropriate to minimize the costs of such resources.
  •  To provide support in testing, training of national fleet management staff, volunteers, and National Societies (NS) to improve the management of quality and cost effectiveness of fleet management operations, promote adherence to best practice principles and compliance with all relevant regulation, legislation and IFRC Fleet Manual
  •  To ensure that the necessary information related to transport/fleet management is effectively shared and communicated to the Sr. Logistics Officer and all other relevant IFRC functions e. g. on driver/vehicle movements/fleet performance/driving safety and accidents
  • Ability to focus and identify high Risk areas and put in place risk management control measures
  •  To support the Country Sr. Logistics Officer in managing, evaluating, and reporting upon fleet management activity/performance to verify the meeting of delivery and quality targets, in-line with GLS and country strategies, and accurate and timely cost information to enable the full recovery of all relevant cost from internal/external service users.
  •  Ensure efficient dispatch of fleet resources to meet program needs in line with standing IFRC fleet manual guidelines ensuring optimum resource utilization
  •  Managing Fleet Assistant, dispatchers, and drivers, providing training, coaching and mentoring as well as all HR related tasks including leave planning, discipline and staff appraisals
  • Work as the main focal point and liaison with all other departments, external and internal stakeholders in all matters relating to the operations of the Federation vehicle fleet

Job Duties and Responsibilities (continued)

  •  Inspecting vehicles and ensuring fleet assets are kept in a serviceable condition in line with fleet manual as revised
  •  Timely scheduling vehicles servicing and working closely with service providers to ensure correct and cost-effective repairing and servicing of vehicle assets
  •  In cooperation with the Service Workshop manager coordinates the inspection, servicing, maintenance, and repair of all vehicles as per policies and procedures. Identifies and recommends where the vehicle condition may impact safe operation and takes remedial action. Authorizes additional repairs as required.
  •  Managing the effective usage of fleet assets logbooks and monitoring the daily, weekly vehicle inspections and vehicle cleaning by drivers and dispatchers
  •  Preparing and obtaining approvals for all transport mission requests and ensuring the appropriate vehicles and drivers are used
  •  Preparing and providing driver per diems for mission movements work advances.
  • Providing Fleet data required for accurate fleet reporting including fleet asset fuel usage, distances travelled and service and maintenance costs
  • Prepare fleet reports as required by the IFRC Country Delegation providing accurate and timely information key for forward planning
  • Prepare monthly fleet report on maintenance, fleet utilization and reconciliation information and data from the Fleet Wave reports and submit to the Sr. Logistics Officer, according to deadlines.
  • Provides critical analysis and evaluation of Fleet Wave data to assist Sr. Logistics Officer with decisions and recommendations on maintenance, servicing, repairs, insurance, disposal and reallocation of vehicles and other motor assets
  • Work closely with NRCS, PNSs and other stakeholders in ensuring close collaboration in fleet management related issues
  • Developing and delivering training to dispatchers and drivers to improve their capacity as well as raise their productivity
  • Prepare documents on import and export requirements of IFRC Country Delegation and its PNSs such as relief items, training kits, vehicles, personal effects, and any other items that is deemed necessary by the Country Delegation.
  •  Coordinate with supply chain stakeholders to ensure the IFRC shipments are shipped and delivered safely and efficiently on time.
  •  Liaise with Government entities MOFA, MOHA, MOF etc. to ensure that the duty exemption facilities are granted for IFRC consignments.
  • Support Sr. Logistics Officer in procurement process of IFRC purchased for internal and development usage.
  • Support Sr. Logistics officer in preparing the monthly logistics reports and circulate with necessary stakeholders.
  • Support Sr. Logistics Officer in maintaining proper files for Procurement, Import/Export and Warehousing elements electronically.
  • Perform any other work-related duties that may be requested by the Sr. Logistics Officer

CWIN-Nepal is seeking a qualified and experienced Child Protection Case Manager to lead the implementation of a child protection project through Child Helpline Nepal 1098.

The Case Manager will provide project leadership and technical supervision for child protection case management, with particular attention to flood-affected children, separated and unaccompanied children, children at risk of gender-based violence, and other vulnerable children requiring special protection.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead overall project implementation, planning, coordination, monitoring, and reporting.
  • Supervise Social Workers and provide regular technical support and case management supervision.
  • Ensure timely identification, assessment, case planning, referral, follow-up, and closure of child protection cases.
  • Support family tracing, reunification, alternative care, and follow-up of separated and unaccompanied children.
  • Coordinate GBV-sensitive and survivor-centred referrals for children requiring specialized services.
  • Strengthen service mapping and referral pathways through Child Helpline Nepal 1098.
  • Coordinate with local governments, Local Child Rights Committees, District Administration Offices, District Coordination Committees, service providers, and relevant child protection mechanisms.
  • Support and engage in capacity-building of Social Workers, frontline workers, and local child protection actors / mechanisms.
  • Ensure accurate case documentation and timely entry and updating of case information in CPIMS.
  • Prepare regular programme reports and support monitoring, review, and learning processes.
  • Ensure compliance with child safeguarding, confidentiality, PSEA, and data protection requirements.

Qualification and Experience

  • Master’s degree in Law, Social Work, Sociology, Psychology, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Child Development, or another relevant field.
  • Candidates with a relevant bachelor’s degree and substantial professional experience may also be considered.
  • Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in child protection, social work, case management, humanitarian response, legal protection, or related programmes.
  • Demonstrated experience in project management, including planning, implementation, team supervision, coordination, monitoring, and reporting.
  • Experience working with vulnerable children, including separated and unaccompanied children, is highly desirable.
  • Knowledge of child rights, child protection legislation, alternative care, GBV response, and referral mechanisms is preferred.
  • Previous experience coordinating with government authorities, local governments, development partners, and service providers will be an advantage.

Required Skills and Personal Attributes

  • Strong project management and team leadership skills.
  • Sound understanding of child protection and relevant legal frameworks.
  • Strong case management, supervision, and decision-making abilities.
  • High level of professional maturity, emotional stability, discretion, and sound judgement.
  • Ability to manage complex and sensitive child protection cases calmly and responsibly.
  • Strong communication, coordination, negotiation, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to maintain strict confidentiality and professional boundaries.
  • Strong report writing, documentation, and computer skills.
  • Ability to work under pressure and respond appropriately during emergencies.
  • Willingness to travel frequently to project areas.

Child Safeguarding

CWIN-Nepal maintains a zero-tolerance approach to child abuse, exploitation, harassment, and sexual exploitation and abuse. The selected candidate must comply with CWIN’s Child Safeguarding, PSEA, Code of Conduct, confidentiality, and data protection policies.

Application Process
