Job Title: Education Specialist – Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL)
Department: Programme
Reports To: Senior Programme Manager
Location: Kathmandu with frequent travel to UWS Nepal programme districts

About UWS Nepal

United World Schools (UWS) Nepal is committed to ensuring that every child has access to quality education and acquires foundational skills required for lifelong learning. UWS Nepal collaborates closely with schools, communities, local governments and education stakeholders to improve educational quality, equity and learning outcomes through Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN), Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL), teacher professional development, instructional leadership, school improvement and education system strengthening initiatives.

Purpose of the Position

The Education Specialist – TaRL will serve as the lead technical resource for the design, implementation, quality assurance and continuous improvement of UWS Nepal’s TaRL approach. The position will support programmes that assess children’s current learning levels, group learners according to ability rather than grade, deliver targeted literacy and numeracy instruction, and use regular assessment data to improve learning outcomes.
The post holder will bring specialist expertise in foundational learning, TaRL methodology, remedial instruction, simple learning assessment, teacher coaching, mentoring, instructional leadership, programme quality improvement and Nepal’s education system.

Key Responsibilities

1. Technical Leadership in TaRL (30%)

  •  Lead the design, contextualisation, implementation and continuous improvement of UWS Nepal’s TaRL approach for foundational literacy and numeracy.
  • Provide technical leadership and guidance to programme teams to ensure TaRL implementation is simple, evidence-informed, child-centred and focused on measurable learning gains.
  •  Develop and refine TaRL tools, routines and teaching-learning activities that strengthen children’s basic reading, comprehension, number sense, arithmetic and problem solving skills.
  •  Ensure TaRL interventions are aligned with national priorities, local government plans, global evidence and UWS education quality frameworks.
  •  Contribute to organisational TaRL strategies, foundational learning frameworks, technical standards and scale-up plans.

 TaRL Pedagogy, Grouping and Learning Improvement (20%)

  •  Provide technical expertise on TaRL pedagogy, level-based grouping, targeted instruction, competency-based learning, and effective classroom practice.
  •  Promote inclusive, child-centred and developmentally appropriate TaRL activities that respond to learners’ current skill levels.
  • Support learning camps, remedial cycles, differentiated instruction and level-wise progression so that children move from basic to more advanced learning groups.
  •  Strengthen classroom practices that use simple activities, peer learning, practice opportunities, and frequent checks for understanding to improve learning outcomes.

 Teacher Professional Development and Instructional Leadership (20%)

  • Design and facilitate TaRL-oriented professional development programmes for teachers, head teachers, education coordinators, mentors, and local education stakeholders.
  • Develop training packages, facilitator guides, practice-based coaching tools, simple assessment protocols and teaching-learning resources for TaRL delivery.
  •  Strengthen systems for TaRL-focused coaching, mentoring, classroom observation, feedback and continuous professional development.
  •  Support instructional leadership initiatives that enable head teachers and education officials to sustain TaRL practices and improve learning outcomes.

TaRL Assessment, Learning Data and Programme Quality (15%)

  • Lead the development and use of simple TaRL assessment tools to identify children’s current learning levels in reading and arithmetic.
  •  Support teachers and programme teams to group children by learning level, track progress regularly and adapt instruction based on assessment results.
  • Analyse TaRL assessment data to identify learning gaps, monitorlearner progression, and inform targeted programme improvements.
  •  Collaborate with programme and MEAL teams to integrate TaRL indicators, monitoring tools and quality assurance processes into programme systems.

Stakeholder Engagement, Knowledge Management and Representation (15%)

  • Serve as UWS Nepal’s technical focal point for TaRL and foundational learning.
  •  Build and maintain effective relationships with government stakeholders, municipalities, schools, development partners, and TaRL technical networks.
  •  Represent UWS Nepal in education forums, technical working groups and sector consultations related to TaRL, FLN and learning recovery.
  •  Document lessons learned, good practices and evidence from TaRL implementation to support programme learning, adaptation and scale-up.

Required Qualifications

Education

  • Master’s degree in Education, Curriculum Studies, Teacher Education, Educational Leadership, Educational Planning, Assessment and Evaluation, Child Development, Literacy, Mathematics Education or related field.
  •  Additional specialization or training in Teaching at the Right Level, FLN, remedial education, teacher professional development, learning assessment or instructional leadership is desirable.

Experience

  •  Minimum 5 years of progressively responsible experience in education programmes, with substantial experience in foundational learning or learning improvement initiatives.
  •  Significant experience in demonstrating foundational learning, TaRL, remedial education or similar level-based learning improvement programmes.
  •  Experience designing and facilitating teacher professional development programmes focused on TaRL, FLN, remedial pedagogy or classroom-based learning improvement.
  •  Experience in learner assessment, level-based grouping, targeted instruction, instructional coaching, and use of data for programme improvement.
  •  Experience working with government education systems, municipalities, schools, NGOs and development partners to implement, monitor or scale learning improvement programmes.

Essential Technical Competencies

TaRL and Foundational Learning

  •  Deep understanding of TaRL principles, foundational literacy and numeracy, and accelerated learning for children who are below grade-level expectations.
  • Level-based grouping, targeted instruction and child-centred TaRL classroom activities.
  •  Basic reading, comprehension, expression, number sense, arithmetic, reasoning and problem-solving.
  •  Simple assessment, learner grouping, progress tracking, and use of assessment data for instruction and course correction.
  • Learning camps, remedial cycles, and practical strategies for helping children progress quickly from their current learning level.

Child Learning, Inclusion and Education Quality

  •  Child development and learning theories.
  •  Early grade and primary education.
  •  Inclusive and child-centered education approaches.
  •  Foundational learning improvement through TaRL, remedial learning, and targeted instruction.
  •  Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI).

Knowledge of Nepal’s Education Sector, including

  •  School Education Sector Plan (SESP).
  • National Curriculum Framework and Basic Education Curriculum.
  • National Strategy for Foundational Learning and relevant TaRL, FLN and learning recovery initiatives.
  •  Teacher Professional Development Framework.
  •  Federal, provincial and local education governance structures.
  •  Functions of CEHRD, CDC, ERO, and local governments.

Teacher Professional Development and Instructional Leadership

  •  Adult learning principles.
  •  Teacher coaching and mentoring for TaRL classroom practice, learner grouping, and use of assessment data.
  • Classroom observation and feedback focused on TaRL routines, learner participation, and progress against learning levels.
  •  School improvement and instructional leadership.

Core Competencies

  •  Strategic Thinking
  •  Technical Leadership
  • Stakeholder Engagement and Influencing
  •  Results Orientation
  •  Planning and Organising
  • Commitment to Equity, Diversity and Inclusion

Safeguarding and Child Protection

The post holder will adhere to UWS Nepal’s Child Protection and Safeguarding Policies and ensure that all programme activities promote child safety, wellbeing, inclusion, dignity and rights. Compliance with safeguarding requirements is mandatory and will be assessed throughout the recruitment process.

Posiiton: Communication Officer
Location: Dhunche, Rasuwa with regular visits to areas of presence
Duration: 6 months with the possibility of extension subject to funding and performance
Reports to: Communication and Advocacy Manager

Introduction

People in Need (PIN) is a non-governmental, non-profit, international organization founded in the Czech Republic in 1992. PIN arrived in Nepal as part of a humanitarian response to the April 25, 2015 earthquake. Since its inception in Nepal, PIN has had a strong role advocating and addressing the needs of marginalized populations. This includes people who live in geographically remote areas of Nepal, people who are from historically marginalized ethnic groups, and those marginalized because of their age and/or gender identity (women and girls). PIN has also supported Nepal’s post-earthquake reconstruction efforts ensuring that the most vulnerable people are not left behind with resilience (focused on shelter and resettlement) and inclusive education programming. PIN-Nepal is strongly committed for safeguarding of children and vulnerable adults, including persons with disabilities, in line with its safeguarding framework and child protection policy.

Scope of work

The Emergency Response Communication Officer will support the visibility, communications, and public information needs of PIN’s emergency response operations in Rasuwa and other affected areas. The position will play a key role in documenting humanitarian interventions, producing high-quality communication materials, collecting human-interest stories, supporting donor visibility requirements, and ensuring timely dissemination of information related to emergency response activities.

Working closely with the Communication and Advocacy Manager, Emergency Response Manager, field teams, and implementing partners, the officer will ensure that emergency response activities are effectively documented and communicated while maintaining humanitarian principles, safeguarding standards, and ethical storytelling practices. S/he will strictly adhere to PIN Code of Conduct and key policies including Media Policy, Child Protection, and Safeguarding Policy.

Task and Responsibilities

Social Media and Media Production

  • Develop engaging content development (in Nepali and English) for PIN Nepal’s digital platforms (websites, microsites) and social media channels (Facebook, Instagram, twitter), including photographs, videos, or multimedia content. S/he is required to coordinate with PIN Nepal’s field team, local staff and partner’s team for necessary local language translation
  • Create postcards, illustrative posts for social media
  • Create infographics for reports, postcards for social media
  • Create content, and regular update of PIN Nepal microsite
  • Take photographs of projects, record audio-visual materials directly in the field, and produce articles, and multimedia content for PIN Nepal microsite and PIN global website based on it
  • Extract ‘stories of change’ and ‘project achievements stories’ from the reports produced by PIN and partners, and produce visibility materials (blogpost, articles, infographic)

  • Assist in preparing training materials

Administrative Tasks

  • Archive the best photos of PIN projects that highlight the organization’s work and values and upload them to Canto with proper captions and photo details
  • Generate ideas and concepts to mark International/National Days and coordinate with PIN teams to execute the ideas

Documentation/Reporting

  • Support in the development of best practices, success stories, and case stories for different projects and interventions
  • Other tasks as assigned by the line manager

REQUIREMENTS

  • Minimum of one year of experience in the relevant field of work, social behavior change communication, journalism, and mass media preferably in media houses or donor-funded related activities.
  • Familiarity with computer skills including knowledge of relevant software like Microsoft Office, photo editing, and video editing tools like Adobe Photoshop,
  • Premiere Pro, InDesign, Canva and Capcut.

COMPETENCIES

  • Excellent interpersonal, communication, and facilitation skills
  • Demonstrated strong competencies in working with various donors, and media, and producing communication and visibility materials
  • Able to present information, and ideas and express opinions confidently to internal and external audiences
  • Excellent verbal and written language skills in both English and Nepali. Other local language(s) is a plus

Position: MEAL Officer– Bhotekoshi Flood Response 2026
Opening: 2 position
Location: Rasuwa based in Dhunche and Kalikasthan
Duration: 1 October 2026 to 28 February 2027
Reports to: MEAL and CFRM Coordinator

Introduction

People in Need (PIN) is a non-governmental, non-profit, international organization founded in the Czech 1992. PIN arrived in Nepal as part of a humanitarian response to the April 25, 2015 earthquake. Since its inception in Nepal, PIN has had a strong role in designing and facilitating systemic solutions advocating for and addressing the needs of vulnerable populations affected by disasters including person categories who live in geographically remote areas of the country, historically marginalized ethnic groups, and those marginalized because of their age and/or gender identity. Currently, PIN Nepal is implementing programmes under three strategic pillars 1) Emergency response and recovery, 2) Climate resilience, and 3) Civil society and inclusive governance. PIN Nepal team works in and promotes strong partnerships with civil society, Government of Nepal, academia, private sector and other key stakeholders in Nepal. Together with them, PIN Nepal has become one of the pioneer organizations advancing programmes such as landslide disaster preparedness and anticipatory action, climate and flood resilient housing, durable local solutions, climate change modelling for more inclusive and efficient local decision-making, girls and inclusive education, waste management and circular economy approaches. PIN is strongly committed for safeguarding of children and vulnerable adults, including persons with disabilities, in line with its safeguarding framework and child protection policy.

Scope of Work

All PIN staff agree to:

  • Comply with all relevant PIN policies, Country Program Policies, and guidelines related to their position.
  • Show a strong commitment to the inclusion of all groups within Nepal and dedication to PIN Nepal’s Inclusion Guidelines.
  •  Perform and accurately complete administrative tasks related to their position.
  • Strive for quality in all aspects of their work and ensure the highest quality performance of the Country Program.
  •  Maintain a positive attitude and promote a professional & productive working environment across all staff, departments, and among all of PIN’s partners.
  • Adhere to PIN Code of Conduct and key policies including Anticorruption Policy, Child Protection Policy and Safeguarding Policy.

About the Project

People in Need (PIN) is implementing an Emergency Flood Response Project in Rasuwa District to provide timely humanitarian assistance to flood-affected communities. The project focuses on addressing immediate humanitarian needs through emergency relief, early recovery support, and the restoration of essential services while ensuring accountability, compliance, and efficient use of resources.

Key Summary of Functions

The MEAL Officer will support the implementation of the MEAL framework for Emergency Flood Response. This includes data collection, monitoring project progress, building partner capacity, and preparing quality reports. The MEAL Officer will maintain clear communication with stakeholders, mainstream Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) in planning and reporting, and uphold PIN Nepal’s safeguarding policies. Additionally, they will utilize PIN’s accountability platform to gather feedback and promote government mechanisms for two-way communication with communities.

Monitoring & Evaluation:

  • Assist in implementing the MEAL framework, including data collection and analysis, to monitor project progress and impact.
  • Conduct regular field visits to monitor project activities, ensuring data quality and adherence to established protocols.
  • Support the design and execution of baseline, mid-term, and end-line evaluations to assess project progress and impact.
  • Utilize both quantitative and qualitative data analysis techniques to generate actionable insights for project improvement.
  • Support in preparation of accurate timely MEAL reports, including progress updates and thematic analyses, to inform decision-making processes.

Accountability:

  • Support the establishment and management of feedback mechanisms to gather input from project beneficiaries and stakeholders, ensuring transparency and responsiveness.
  • Monitor the effectiveness of feedback systems and ensure that community concerns are addressed promptly.
  • Facilitate community engagement sessions to validate findings and promote ownership of project outcomes.

Learning:

  • Document and disseminate best practices, lessons learned, and success stories to promote organizational learning and inform future programming.
  •  Organize and facilitate learning events, workshops, and knowledge-sharing sessions with project staff and stakeholders.
  • Support the integration of MEAL findings into project planning and implementation to ensure adaptive management.

Capacity Building:

  •  Provide training and technical support to enumerators and partners on MEAL methodologies, data management, and analysis.
  • Strengthen the capacity of field teams to implement MEAL activities effectively and ensure data quality.

Information Management:

  •  Support to maintain project databases to ensure accurate and accessible data storage.
  • Ensure that data collection tools are appropriately designed and utilized across project sites.
  • Promote the use of data for decision-making and continuous improvement within project teams.

Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) Mainstreaming:

  •  Ensure GEDSI considerations are integrated into all MEAL activities and project planning.
  • Highlight GEDSI-related results in monitoring and evaluation plans and reflect them in reporting.
  • Ensure the project activities are planned and implemented in a gender-sensitive and inclusive manner and that all implementing partners are sensitized and trained in monitoring and reporting of gender and social inclusion-sensitive results.

Community Feedback and Response Mechanism (CFRM):

  • Utilize PIN’s existing accountability platform (Community Feedback Response Mechanism – CFRM) and promote government accountability platforms to receive community feedback and foster two-way communication with the community/stakeholders.
  • Adhere to PIN-Nepal’s policies, guidance, and procedures, with special attention to safeguarding standards and procedures, case handling framework, child protection, and Do No Harm policies; immediate

Education

Experience

  • Minimum 2 years of professional experience in monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning, preferably within humanitarian, emergency response, disaster management, or development projects.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting MEAL systems for emergency response projects, including data collection, analysis, reporting, and database management.
  • Proven experience in conducting monitoring visits, beneficiary feedback mechanisms, post-distribution monitoring (PDM), assessments, and data quality assurance.
  • Strong skills in data analysis and visualization using Excel and other data management tools; knowledge of Power BI or similar software is an asset.
  • Experience working with local authorities, communities, and humanitarian coordination mechanisms in Nepal is an advantage.

OBJECTIVES OF THE PROGRAMME

The WHO Report on the Global Tobacco Epidemic (GTCR) is published every two years and for the last 18 years has successfully tracked the progress in tobacco control across all Member States. The next report, the eleventh in the series, will be published in 2027. The GTCR is one of WHO’s flagship publications and is supported by Bloomberg Philanthropies.

DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES

Under the supervision of a technical expert in the respective area, the intern is assigned the agreed terms of reference:

  • proofread and cross-check drafts and revisions
  • conduct an independent data validation on all analyses reported in the report
  • undertake web research and data collection on specific subject areas
  • organize and validate data and documents
  • assist in organizing the launch of the report
  • participate in on-going departmental projects

Learning objectives
The purpose of the WHO Internship Programme is to provide an enriching learning experience for students and recent graduates. The Learning Objectives outlined within each internship vacancy are a key component of the programme.

Within this internship, the intern will:

  • Understand the objectives of the programme/area of work
  • Communicate clearly about the programme/area of work
  • Understand the global status of tobacco control policies
  • Understand the role of monitoring policy progress in global health
  • Communicate clearly about the programme/area of work
  • Know how to assemble data and prepare a comprehensive analysis
  • Communicate clearly and effectively between stakeholders to ensure the production of a high-quality global report
  • Understand the difference of work between headquarters, regional offices and country offices

DURATION OF INTERNSHIP 

1 February 2027- 16 July 2027

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

Education

Have completed the equivalent of three years of full-time studies in a health or data-science related subject at a university or equivalent institution prior to commencing the assignment; AND be enrolled in a course of study at a university or equivalent institution leading to a formal qualification (applicants who have already graduated may also qualify for consideration provided that they apply to the internship within eighteen months after completion of their formal qualification).

Skills

Core competencies

  • Team work
  • Respecting and promoting individual and cultural differences
  • Communication

All interns should be able to demonstrate the following skills in line with the WHO core competencies:

  • Communicating effectively orally and in writing
  • Showing willingness to learn from mistakes
  • Producing and delivering quality results
  • Working collaboratively with team members

In addition, interns need to be familiar with commonly used computer programmes, such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint. Knowledge of specialized computer programmes, for example, statistical software may be an advantage.

Experience

  • Experience in research and/or in drafting reports
  • Experience in the subject area through academic work or research
  • Experience with data analysis, statistical packages and interest in the design of graphical display and analysis of health information in an international comparative perspective, such as for health system performance assessment
  • More specific experience such as specialized computer programmes

Languages

Essential: Expert knowledge of English.
Desirable: Intermediate knowledge of other UN language.

FINANCIAL SUPPORT

Interns do not receive a salary. They do however receive a living allowance. The amount of living allowance is different in each duty station. The amount also depends on any other external financial support received by the intern (grant, scholarships, etc.) and whether their permanent residence is in the duty station of the internship. In Geneva, for interns with permanent residence in the duty station, the maximum amount of the allowance provided by WHO is 739 CHF per month. For interns whose permanent residence is outside of the duty station, the maximum amount is 1680 CHF per month. The exact amount of the living allowance will be calculated for each intern, after selection, based on a legal financial disclosure form that the individual will complete. In addition, all interns in Geneva will receive  daily lunch vouchers for meal expenses (20 CHF per working day). WHO also provides all interns with accident and medical insurance coverage.


ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

  • Please note that internships at WHO are very competitive and only a small number of applicants will be accepted every year. Only candidates under serious consideration will be contacted.
  • Living abroad is expensive and finding accommodation can be challenging. All intern candidates should be aware of these factors before they consider applying for a WHO Internship.
  • If selected for a WHO Internship, candidates will be required to provide certified copies of proof of enrolment in an eligible course of studies, a completed WHO medical certificate of fitness for work, and the contact details for reference checks.
  • WHO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU)/United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). The list can be accessed through the link: http://www.whed.net. Some professional certificates may not appear in the WHED and will require individual review.
  • WHO prides itself on a workforce that adheres to the highest ethical and professional standards and that is committed to put the WHO Values Charter into practice.
  • WHO has zero tolerance towards sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA), sexual harassment and other types of abusive conduct (i.e., discrimination, abuse of authority and harassment). All members of the WHO workforce have a role to play in promoting a safe and respectful workplace and should report to WHO any actual or suspected cases of SEA, sexual harassment and other types of abusive conduct. To ensure that individuals with a substantiated history of SEA, sexual harassment or other types of abusive conduct are not hired by the Organization, WHO will conduct a background verification of final candidates.
  • The WHO is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. The WHO recruits and employs staff regardless of disability status, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, language, race, marital status, religious, cultural, ethnic and socio-economic backgrounds, or any other personal characteristics.
  • The WHO is committed to achieving gender parity and geographical diversity in its workforce. Women, persons with disabilities, and nationals of unrepresented and underrepresented Member States (https://www.who.int/careers/diversity-equity-and-inclusion) are strongly encouraged to apply.
  • Persons with disabilities can request reasonable accommodations to enable participation in the recruitment process. Requests for reasonable accommodation should be sent through an email to reasonableaccommodation@who.int
  • WHO has a smoke-free environment and does not recruit smokers or users of any form of tobacco.
  • Please note that WHO’s contracts are conditional on members of the workforce confirming that they are vaccinated as required by WHO before undertaking a WHO assignment, except where a medical condition does not allow such vaccination, as certified by the WHO Department of Staff Health and Wellbeing (SHW). The successful candidate will be asked to provide relevant evidence related to this condition. A copy of the updated vaccination card must be shared with WHO medical service in the medical clearance process. Please note that certain countries require proof of specific vaccinations for entry or exit. For example, official proof /certification of yellow fever vaccination is required to enter many countries. Posiiton: Roving Logistics and IT Officer
Location: Based in Kathmandu with frequent travel to Emergency Flood Response area( Rasuwa and other areas)
Reports to: IT and Logistics Lead based in Kathmandu

Introduction

People in Need (PIN) is a non-governmental, non-profit, international organization founded in the Czech 1992. PIN arrived in Nepal as part of a humanitarian response to the April 25, 2015 earthquake. Since its inception in Nepal, PIN has had a strong role in designing and facilitating systemic solutions advocating for and addressing the needs of vulnerable populations affected by disasters including person categories who live in geographically remote areas of the country, historically marginalized ethnic groups, and those marginalized because of their age and/or gender identity. Currently, PIN Nepal is implementing programmes under three strategic pillars 1) Emergency response and recovery, 2) Climate resilience, and 3) Civil society and inclusive governance. PIN Nepal team works in and promotes strong partnerships with civil society, Government of Nepal, academia, private sector and other key stakeholders in Nepal. Together with them, PIN Nepal has become one of the pioneer organizations advancing programmes such as landslide disaster preparedness and anticipatory action, climate and flood resilient housing, durable local solutions, climate change modelling for more inclusive and efficient local decision-making, girls and inclusive education, waste management and circular economy approaches. PIN is strongly committed for safeguarding of children and vulnerable adults, including persons with disabilities, in line with its safeguarding framework and child protection policy.

Scope of Work

Logistics and IT Officer is member of support department who manages supports the logistics functions and provide the IT supports to of field based staff and its office in close coordination with Program team, field office staff and other respective departments for the effective delivery IT and logistics support functions. S/he will be in charge of managing Assets and warehouse (Stock/Inventory) in line with logistics operating procedures. S/he will work Closely with IT and Logistics Lead based in Kathmandu for IT related works. This includes but is not limited to the following roles and responsibilities. This is a roving position expected to travel to affected areas as per project need.

Key Job Responsibilities

Procurement and supply chain management- 40%

  • Support purchasing functions of goods and services in compliance with PIN, donors and government regulations under supervision of Operations Lead.
  • Support to the programme team to raise and compile Purchase Request Form (PRF) to proceeds the procurement under the supervision of Operations Lead.
  • Support to Request for Quotation (RFQ) and Tender documents in close coordination with Operations Lead.
  • Coordinate to build professional liaison and coordination with potential suppliers and collect quotations/bids as required.
  • Assist the Operations Lead in conducting market research and ensure best value for money while purchasing goods and services.
  • Update procurement status tracking sheet, supplier’s database and contracts regularly.
  • Prepare purchase request and purchase order for the procurement of goods and services.
  • Managed to archive procurement documents in ELO regularly.
  • Coordinate with finance, field programme team to sort out procurement related issues if any in close coordination with Operations Lead.
  • Support domestic and regional Flight tickets as per the request of staff.

IT management- 25%

  • Support IT functions of People In Need at field offices in close coordination with IT and Logistics Lead based in Kathmandu office.
  • Installation of Laptops with PIN image, KPP installation, manage WIFI-vouchers, and connect the laptops to Microsoft Entra ID (previously known as Active Azure Directory).
  • Support general IT related troubleshooting of staff like; fixing laptops, printer, network, email, internet as per request.
  • Oversee IT facilities and keep them always updated, functional and maintained on time i.e networking, internet, data security, etc.
  • In charge of managing IT equipment and regular repair and maintenance to keep them in good working condition at all times.
  • Manage to provide IT equipment needed for new staff.
  • Keep proper movement record of IT related equipment
  • Coordinate with NPL IT and Logistics Lead for IT functions as required and sort out the issue if any.

Customs Clearance and Importation Support-5%

  • Coordinate and support customs clearance processes for imported relief items, equipment, and project supplies in compliance with Government of Nepal regulations and donor requirements
  • Liaise with customs authorities, freight forwarders, clearing agents, and relevant government stakeholders to facilitate timely clearance of humanitarian cargo.
  • Prepare and maintain customs-related documentation, including exemption requests, import permits, packing lists, invoices, and supporting documents.
  • Track incoming international shipments and ensure timely receipt and delivery to project locations
  • Maintain proper records and filing of all customs and importation documents
  • complete tasks as required

Warehouse (Stock/Inventory) management- 20%

  • Support in managing warehouse and ensure its facilities are well maintained and utilities are working well.
  • Support in ensuring warehousing equipment are in good working conditions at all times.
  • Ensure safe storage and security of stocks.

Posiiton: Procurement and Logistics Manager
Duty Station: Kathmandu, Nepal, with regular travel to field locations
Reports to: Head of System and Operations (HoSO)
Department: Operations
Contract/Assignment: Initially 6 months
Priority Assignment: Rasuwa Flood Response during the initial six months

Introduction

People in Need (PIN) is a non-governmental, non-profit, international organization founded in the Czech 1992. PIN arrived in Nepal as part of a humanitarian response to the April 25, 2015 earthquake. Since its inception in Nepal, PIN has had a strong role in designing and facilitating systemic solutions advocating for and addressing the needs of vulnerable populations affected by disasters including person categories who live in geographically remote areas of the country, historically marginalized ethnic groups, and those marginalized because of their age and/or gender identity. Currently, PIN Nepal is implementing programmes under three strategic pillars 1) Emergency response and recovery, 2) Climate resilience, and 3) Civil society and inclusive governance. PIN Nepal team works in and promotes strong partnerships with civil society, Government of Nepal, academia, private sector and other key stakeholders in Nepal. Together with them, PIN Nepal has become one of the pioneer organizations advancing programmes such aslandslide disaster preparedness and anticipatory action, climate and flood resilient housing, durable local solutions, climate change modelling for more inclusive and efficient local decision-making, girls and inclusive education, waste management and circular economy approaches. PIN is strongly committed for safeguarding of children and vulnerable adults, including persons with disabilities, in line with its safeguarding framework and child protection policy.

Scope of Work

Lead and coordinate end-to-end logistics and procurement operations for the Rasuwa Flood Response, ensuring timely, compliant and cost-effective delivery of relief assistance. The role covers procurement planning and supplier management, warehouse and inventory management, transportation and fleet coordination, customs and relief item clearance, asset management, and field logistics support. It also includes coordination with programme, finance, HR, security and field teams; oversight of logistics documentation and controls; support to emergency distributions and staff movements; and regular travel to Rasuwa to assess and address operational needs. The position ensures that logistics activities comply with PIN policies, emergency SOPs, donor requirements and applicable Nepalese regulations.

All PIN staff agree to:

  • Comply with all relevant PIN policies, Country Program Policies, and guidelines related to their position.•Show a strong commitment to the inclusion of all groups within Nepal and dedication to PIN Nepal’s Inclusion Guidelines.
  • Perform and accurately complete administrative tasks related to their position.
  • Strive for quality in all aspects of their work and ensure the highest quality performance of the Country Program.
  • Maintain a positive attitude and promote a professional & productive working environment across all staff, departments, and among all of PIN’s partners.
  • Adhere to PIN Code of Conduct and key policies including Anticorruption Policy, Child Protection Policy and Safeguarding Policy.

About the Project

People in Need (PIN) is implementing an Emergency Flood Response Project in Rasuwa District to provide timely humanitarian assistance to flood-affected communities. The project focuses on addressing immediate humanitarian needs through emergency relief, early recovery support, and the restoration of essential services while ensuring accountability, compliance, and efficient use of resources.

Key Summary of Functions

The Procurement and Logistics Manager will provide leadership, coordination and technical oversight of procurement, logistics and supply chain functions across PIN Nepal, ensuring the timely, efficient and compliant procurement, movement, storage and delivery of goods, services, equipment and relief materials. During the initial six months, the position will have a particular focus on the Rasuwa Flood Response, providing hands-on coordination and technical support to emergency procurement, supply chain, transportation, warehousing, customs clearance and field logistics. The position will also contribute to strengthening country-level procurement and logistics systems, staff capacity and supply chain visibility. The role requires a good understanding of the Nepal humanitarian and operational context, including local markets, suppliers, geographical and access constraints, transportation, government processes and emergency operating environments.

Procurement and Supply Chain Management

  • Lead and coordinate procurement and supply chain activities across PIN Nepal in close coordination with Finance, Programme, HR, Security and management teams.•Ensure timely procurement and availability of goods, services, equipment and relief materials in line with programme and operational requirements.
  • Support procurement planning, specifications, market research, supplier identification, quotation processes and supplier management.Ensure procurement processes are competitive, transparent, properly documented and compliant with PIN policies, donor requirements and applicable Government of Nepal regulations.
  • Maintain visibility of procurement pipelines and identify and resolve bottlenecks, delays and supply risks.

Rasuwa Emergency Response and Field Logistics

  • Lead procurement and logistics coordination for the Rasuwa Flood Response during the initial assignment period.•Coordinate the emergency supply chain from procurement/importation through customs, warehousing, transportation, field storage and delivery/distribution.
  • Coordinate closely with Rasuwa field teams, Kathmandu-based teams, Programme, Finance, Security and senior management to ensure uninterrupted supply and operational support.
  • Regularly travel to Rasuwa and other field locations to monitor operations, strengthen systems and provide practical technical support.
  • Apply knowledge of the local emergency context, markets, access, infrastructure and operating environment to support effective and timely logistics solutions.
  • Provide surge support during periods of high workload, emergency escalation or staff capacity gaps.

Warehouse, Transport, Fleet and Customs

  • Oversee warehouse, stock, transportation, fleet and logistics arrangements supporting programme and emergency operations.
  • Ensure appropriate receipt, storage, stock control, physical verification, dispatch and documentation of programme and relief materials.
  • Coordinate transportation requirements, including route planning, loading, dispatch, delivery and receipt, while monitoring costs, schedules and vehicle utilisation.
  • Coordinate customs clearance and import facilitation, including liaison with customs agents, suppliers and relevant Government of Nepal authorities.
  • Support the establishment and strengthening of field offices, warehouses, guesthouses, fleet and other operational arrangements as required.

Compliance and Approval Process

  • Work closely with Finance to ensure budget availability, appropriate financial documentation and proper financial controls within procurement and logistics activities.•Ensure procurement requests and transactions follow the applicable PIN ELO approval process, including appropriate initiation, review, approval and supporting documentation before commitments or purchases are made.
  • Ensure appropriate segregation of duties, approval levels and emergency procurement procedures are maintained.Promote timely and accurate documentation for procurement, payments, advances, transport, warehouse and other logistics transactions.
  • Conduct or coordinate compliance checks and support audits, donor verification, due diligence and other compliance reviews.
  • Contribute to the development and updating of procurement, logistics and emergency SOPs, tools and guidance.

Team Leadership and Capacity Building

  • Provide functional and technical supervision, coaching and guidance to procurement and logistics staff as assigned.•Ensure clear roles, responsibilities and effective coordination between Kathmandu and field-based teams.
  • Identify capacity gaps and support training, mentoring and onboarding of procurement and logistics staff.
  • Promote teamwork, accountability, timely communication and effective coordination across operations.
  • Support recruitment and operational deployment of procurement and logistics staff when required.

Planning, Reporting and Risk Management

  • Maintain regular visibility of procurement pipelines, stock levels, transportation, customs clearance and key supply chain risks.•Provide timely management information, analysis and updates to the line manager and HQ.
  • Identify procurement, logistics and operational risks and recommend practical mitigation measures.
  • Contribute to operational planning, contingency planning and the transition from emergency surge arrangements toward sustainable country-level systems.
  • Escalate critical procurement, logistics, financial or supply chain issues in a timely manner.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Master’s degree in procurement, supply chain management, logistics, business administration, finance, management or a related field.•At least 8 years of relevant professional experience in procurement, logistics, supply chain or operations, preferably within an INGO, humanitarian or development organisation. Minimum 3-4 years in senior level.
  • Experience with procurement, warehousing, transportation, fleet and/or customs clearance, with an understanding of their integration with financial management.
  • Experience supervising, coaching or supporting teams across different locations.
  • Strong coordination, negotiation, planning and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work under pressure and manage competing priorities in an emergency environment.Willingness and ability to travel regularly to Rasuwa and other field locations.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills in English and Nepali.
  • Proficiency in MS Office and relevant procurement, logistics or ERP systems.

Required Experience and Knowledge

  • Experience supporting emergency or flood response operations in Nepal, with a good understanding of the local humanitarian, geographical, market and operational context.
  • Practical understanding of ongoing flood-response logistics, including supply movement, transportation, warehousing, field access and coordination with local stakeholders.
  • Understanding of basic INGO financial management, including budget control, procurement-related payments, advances, supporting documentation and financial compliance.
  • Familiarity with digital approval workflows, ERP systems and procurement management systems.

1. Background

  •  Chaudhary Foundation is implementing disaster relief and recovery activities in flood affected districts following the recent flood disaster. The organization requires a capable and experienced Admin Cum Social Mobilizer to support field administration, community mobilization, local coordination, store management and local procurement, ensuring smooth day-to-day operation of the field office.

2. Key Responsibilities

  •  Manage day-to-day administrative activities of the field office and support smooth project operations.
  •  Mobilize and coordinate with affected communities, local representatives, ward offices and other local stakeholders.
  •  Maintain regular communication and local liaison with communities, local authorities, supporters and service providers.
  •  Support identification of community needs and facilitate communication between communities and the project team.
  •  Maintain proper records of field office correspondence, attendance, meetings, logistics and administrative documents.
  •  Manage the field store, including receiving, issuing, recording and monitoring project materials and supplies.
  • Maintain stock registers and ensure proper storage and accountability of materials and equipment.
  •  Support local purchasing of materials, goods and services in accordance with organizational procedures.
  •  Collect quotations, coordinate with local vendors, and support purchase documentation and comparative statements as required.
  •  Monitor availability of essential materials and inform management of procurement or logistical requirements.
  •  Support field staff with accommodation, transportation, meetings and other administrative/logistical arrangements.
  •  Prepare regular administrative, procurement, store and social mobilization updates/reports.

3. Social Mobilization & Local Liaison

  • Build and maintain positive relationships with affected households and local communities.
  •  Facilitate community meetings, consultations and awareness activities.
  •  Coordinate with local government, ward representatives, community leaders and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Support transparent and inclusive implementation of relief and recovery activities.
  •  Identify local concerns, grievances and operational issues and communicate them to the project team.

4. Required Qualification & Experience

  • Bachelor’s Degree in any discipline/stream.
  • Proven experience in a similar administrative, social mobilization, field coordination or humanitarian/disaster-response role.
  •  Experience in disaster relief, recovery, community development or NGO/INGO projects will be highly preferred.
  • Experience in local procurement, store management and field administration will be an advantage.
  • Experience working with local communities and government stakeholders is preferred.

5. Required Skills & Competencies

  •  Ability to work independently in a remote and challenging post-disaster environment.
  •  Strong communication, coordination and interpersonal skills.
  •  Good community mobilization and local liaison skills.
  •  Good coministration, record-keeping and organizational abilities.
  • Basic to good knowledge of MS Word and Excel.
  •  Ability to maintain accurate store, procurement and administrative records and documents.
  • Good negotiation and coordination skills for local purchasing and vendor management.
  •  Honest, responsible, proactive and able to work under pressure.

6. Local Candidate Preference

  • Preference will be given to a qualified local candidate from nearby areas with good knowledge of the local community, geography, language, market conditions and local stakeholders. Local candidates with proven experience in disaster-response or community-based projects will be particularly encouraged to apply.

7. Reporting

The selected candidate will report to the designated Project/Program Coordinator and will coordinate closely with the Site Engineer/Field Team Leader and other field staff. The position will be responsible for ensuring smooth administration, community coordination, store management and local procurement at the field level

To apply, send us your resume at khusbu.shakya@chaudharygroup.com with a well stated subject line for the position.

Opening: 1 position (based in CSO)

Location: Karnali Province, Surkhet

Duration: One year (with possibility of extension)

Reports to: Project Manager (PM)

Introduction

People in Need (PIN) is a non-governmental, non-profit, international organisation founded in the Czech 1992. PIN arrived in Nepal as part of a humanitarian response to the April 25, 2015 earthquake. Since its inception in Nepal, PIN has had a strong role in designing and facilitating systemic solutions, advocating for and addressing the needs of vulnerable populations affected by disasters, including people who live in geographically remote areas of the country, historically marginalised ethnic groups, and those marginalised because of their age and/or gender identity. Currently, PIN Nepal is implementing programmes under three strategic pillars: 1) Emergency response and recovery, 2) Climate resilience, and 3) Civil society and inclusive governance. PIN Nepal team works in and promotes strong partnerships with civil society, the Government of Nepal, academia, the private sector and other key stakeholders in Nepal. Together with them, PIN Nepal has become one of the pioneer organisations advancing programmes such as landslide disaster preparedness and anticipatory action, climate and flood resilient housing, durable local solutions, climate change modelling for more inclusive and efficient local decision-making, girls and inclusive education, waste management and circular economy approaches. PIN is strongly committed to the safeguarding of children and vulnerable adults, including persons with disabilities, in line with its safeguarding framework and child protection policy.

Scope of Work

Under the direct supervision of the Project Manager, the Provincial Coordinator will support the project team in the effective implementation of the related activities under the ACCESS project and represent PIN at Provincial and local/district levels. This includes supporting the program, M&E department, and partners’ staff and district chapters in the implementation of project deliverables in the field. S/he will be responsible for the management of activity trackers and information sharing across the organisation, partners and other relevant stakeholders. Additionally, PC will work together with the GIEN lead and GIEN officers.

All PIN staff agree to:

  • Comply with all relevant PIN policies, Country Program Policies, and guidelines related to their position.
  • Show a strong commitment to the inclusion of all groups within Nepal and dedication to PIN Nepal’s Inclusion Guidelines.
  • Perform and accurately complete administrative tasks related to their position.
  • Strive for quality in all aspects of their work and ensure the highest quality performance of the Country Program.
  • Maintain a positive attitude and promote a professional & productive working environment across all staff, departments, and among all of PIN’s partners.
  • Adhere to PIN Code of Conduct and key policies including Anti-Corruption Policy, Child Protection Policy and Safeguarding Policy.

About the Project

ACCESS – Accelerating Civil Society’s Role in Securing Education for All in Madhesh, Karnali and Sudurpaschim Provinces _ ACCESS programme

People in Need (PIN), the National Campaign for Education (NCE), the Nepal Disabled Women Association (NDWA), and Accountability Lab Nepal (ALN) have collaborated to develop a comprehensive, locally-driven initiative in the Madhesh, Karnali, and Sudurpaschim provinces. This initiative aims to strengthen the role of civil society in ensuring education for all by empowering CSOs and networks to lead the implementation of the School Education Sector Plan (SESP). The consortium will partner with member CSOs of NCE and NDWA to (i) enhance their organisational and technical capacities in implementing inclusive education methodologies, and (ii) provide local CSOs with the skills to promote transparency and accountability in education plans through the mobilisation of Girls and Inclusive Education Networks (GIEN) and the CivActs model. The EU-funded ACCESS project is scheduled to begin implementation on April 1, 2024. It is expected that this program will directly benefit community members, Community-Based Organisations (CBOs), Civil Society Organisations (CSOs), and government tiers across the three provinces, including community schools, by strengthening civil society’s role and improving participation in advancing equitable access to education. The priority provinces for this initiative are Madhesh, Karnali, and Sudurpaschim.

Key Summary of Functions

  • Support the PM in managing project implementation at the field level, jointly with consortium partners, in line with the proposal strategies and donor requirements; also work with the GIEN lead, GIEN officers, and related project team members to scale up GIEN and related interventions.
  • Establish and ensure good partnership with key partners and stakeholders in the implementation at the province and district level
  • Support the PM to lead adaptive management and a facilitation approach within the project.
  • Support PM to ensure systematic and effective capturing of sector-specific results, including programmatic outputs/outcomes and longer-term impact, through sound M&E mechanisms.
  • Engage with PM to provide timely feedback to the programme team determining programmatic adaptations/modifications in response where appropriate;
  • Ensure proper risk mapping of project activities and implement mitigation measures, including the sound Safeguarding strategy and risk analysis at field level;
  • Coordinate closely with other SESP and education implementing agencies, including SAVE, UNICEF, NDWA, NCE, ALN, Government of Nepal, and/or any other stakeholders at the field level.

Project Implementation

  • Assist in the development and oversee the implementation of project interventions under the project at the field level
  • Provide guidance and support to the Project Manager for implementing partners that include, but not limited to, planning, budgeting/forecasting/tracking and implementing planned activities, reviewing the progress including preparing periodic reports, developing case studies/transforming the lives/success stories, and documenting the entire process.
  • Work jointly with the GIEN lead, including project team members at the field level and closely with NCE/NDWA/ALN provincial and district project teams that include related chapters.
  • Provide technical support to carry out the capacity development and community engagement activities with/for partners, communities and local stakeholders that are directly linked with project activities, including Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) grants.
  • Coordinate with M&E department, programs department, local partners, and external evaluation partner to ensure regular program monitoring and evaluation.
  • Support the Project Manager to work with finance to make sure that all finance-related work is following the financial requirements of the project.
  • Coordinate with relevant government and non-government agencies/ organizations to ensure optimum elaboration, reducing duplication and maximising the result at the field level.
  • Produce written reports on activities and outcomes (monthly, quarterly and annually) and submit to the Project Manager.
  • Ensure safeguarding of children, vulnerable groups (including people with disabilities) and those in fragile and conflict-affected states at all times.
  • Act as a focal point to support PIN communication, linkage and sustainability at the field level.
  • Ensure clear communication flow and coordination between PIN, Partners and Government Stakeholders, other partners, and beneficiaries and represent in provincial forums.
  • Support and assist PIN’s MEAL department, programs department, local partners, and external evaluation partner to ensure regular program monitoring, evaluation and learning.
  • Provide leadership to provincial partner chapters and to the programme team, offering guidance, support, and ensuring the quality of project delivery is understood and upheld by all team members.

Representation and Networking

  • Ensure that PIN is well represented and visible within the donor community, among the consortia and stakeholders, mostly in provincial and district (clusters, local/provincial/ government, AIN working groups)
  • Support PM and, together with the MEAL Manager, Partnership Manager and Communication & Advocacy Manager, engage in project-learning-based PIN’s positioning and advocacy, development of learning papers and selection of advocacy points, engage in advocacy and policy dialogues where appropriate in provincial/district.
  • Liaise with concerned government stakeholders and other existing partners in the assigned province, district, Rural Municipality, and Community, and maintain healthier professional relationships.
  • Provide support to the Project Managers/GIEN lead and partners to organize provincial / district level/local level/orientation/induction in relation to the ACCESS project.
  • Communicate regularly with PM and project team, including MEAL, safeguarding, GEDSI and ensure project visibility, working closely with the Communication team.
  • Timely communicate/report to Child Protection Focal Person to ensure safeguarding of child/adult at risk.

Mainstreaming and Quality Management

  • Support PM mainstreaming and strengthening of GEDSI, GBV mitigation, climate change, DRR and safeguarding agendas within programme planning and implementation;
  • Assist PM and work closely with ACCESS MEAL Coordinator, MEAL Manager and team to ensure that project-based learnings and monitoring/evaluation results are regularly used and reflected in PIN’s work;
  • Ensure and strengthen quality focus within the project, across all cross-cutting components at the field level.

Program Operations Management

  • Assist the Project Manager in operational management of the project, including following financial, admin, logistics, and communications tasks to ensure full compliance with PIN’s and donors’ financial and procurement procedures.
  • Work closely with the Project Manager to ensure that partners comply with contractual obligations.
  • Lead, along with the M&E unit, to ensure that the partners are on track in terms of meeting deadlines and producing quantitative and qualitative deliverables.
  • Monitor and support the Child Protection focal person to monitor field staff and partners’ adherence to PIN’s policies and internal procedures, protocols, PIN’s Code of Conduct, with special attention to Safeguarding Standards and Procedure, Case Handling Framework, Child Protection, safeguarding and Do No Harm policies; immediate reporting and redress of any complaints and issues based on their severity.
  • Ensure Branding and Marketing is well reflected and is practised in all activities as guided by the EU-ACCESS and PIN’s Communication Guideline.

Requirements

  • Master’s degree in education, social science/work, rural development, or relevant field, with at least 3 years of demonstrated work experience or Bachelor’s degree with 5 years of work experience with an I/NGO in the following areas:
  • Knowledge and engagement/implementation of SESP and ReAL, inclusive education, engagement in provincial AIN, clusters and relevant forums, working/handling CSOs and partnership skills will be value added
  • Knowledge of working modality with MUAN, NARMIN, province-level GIEN, SMC and PTA federations and their mobilisation
  • Technical capacities to implement inclusive education methodologies and approaches and mobilisation, including strengthening of CSOs, Transparency and accountability of education plans across Local Government (LGs)

  • Local language proficiency (Bajika, Bhojpuri, Maithili, Tharu) will be a plus.

Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. Organizational Context

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability.

IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe.

The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles.

The IFRC is currently present in Nepal through a Country Delegation (CD – first established in 1965 with a presence through regional representation at times), providing support to Nepal Red Cross Society (NRCS) programmes and National Society development (NSD) amongst as well as emergency response, other areas. The longer-term mission of the Nepal Delegation is to facilitate organisational growth, technical capacities, partnerships, and resource mobilisation that enable Nepal Red Cross Society to deliver on its humanitarian mandate in the country through the provision of technical support, advocacy, representation and coordination functions, in accordance with Strategy 2030, the IFRC Renewal and annual Operational Plans.

The Country Delegation also provides integration services to six IFRC members with a presence in Nepal.

On 26 August 2026, a major ice-rock avalanche occurred in the upper Bhote Koshi watershed near the China–Nepal border, resulting in an historically powerful flash flood that advanced from the border down the entire length of Nepal along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli River basins.

Due to the evolving operational requirements of the Rasuwa Flash Flood 2026 response operation, this role profile provides an overview of the principal responsibilities and functions associated with this position within a Federation-coordinated operation.

Job Purpose

Senior Officer, Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) is a member who supports the IFRC’s programmatic vision for WASH and its translation into programmatic interventions, in close collaboration and coordination with NSs, by providing technical advice, support and coordination to the Federation’s programmes in the area of WASH throughout the resilience continuum (in emergency, recovery and development contexts).

The person will be the principal representative in executing the WASH activities at field level and report to Operations Manager. The main objective of the Sr. WASH Officer is to establish strong coordination among stakeholders and linkages with NRCS technical leads in the field to ensure that program activities are implemented successfully.

Job Duties and Responsibilities

Enable RCRC to be a global leading player in the WASH sector

  • Contribute to and support the coordination of the work of RCRC at relevant regional, ensuring interventions are in line with global and regional strategic directions and advocacy themes.
  • Contribute to the development of global policies, strategies, guidelines and tools as well as the integration of these standards into the work of RCRC to ensure sound and sustainable WASH programmes and effective public health outcomes.
  • Work closely with other members of the WASH team and relevant colleagues at the IFRC CCSTs/COs, contributing to ensuring appropriate visibility, resource mobilization and public awareness of the work of IFRC/RCRC.

Support NSs to improve its emergency WASH performance

  • Support the mapping of regional WASH programming, progress and best practices and priority needs of NSs especially in the context of emergency WASH and contribute to the development of project and programme proposals in line with best practice.
  • Work closely with NSs and provide technical guidance to the planning process of emergency WASH activities.
  • Contribute to providing specific technical support to ensure NSs are able to effectively incorporate WASH components/elements within each stage of the emergency cycle and along the resilience continuum: strengthening of WASH as part of prevention; WASH disaster preparedness; water quality monitoring as part of community disease detection and early warning; emergency WASH response including full spectrum of public health related WASH capacities and WASH during recovery aimed at ‘building back better’.
  • Contribute to the four cross organizational WASH related work streams: WASH for development through expansion of GWSI; WASH in disasters; WASH during public health emergencies and WASH in Urban Settings.

Contribute to and backstop coordination of WASH during emergencies

  • Provide technical input to emergency plans of action and engage with implementing NSs to support operations as appropriate including supporting the selection and deployment of surge personnel.
  • When required and in line with other work priorities be available for direct deployment to support emergency response for up to 1 month.

Contribute to delivering quality emergency WASH programming

  • Take an active role in the preparation and facilitation of related trainings organised by IFRC CCSTs/COs and NSs. Training preparation could include working on training modules/content, aligned with global policies, strategies, guidelines and tools, and strategies/priorities of the NSs.
  • Contribute to the development of tools and guidelines in accordance with applicable international standards to enhance the quality of operations, and eventual dissemination to NSs and IFRC CCSTs/COs.
  • Working in close collaboration with NSs and IFRC CCSTs/COs to put in place, where relevant and appropriate, a systematic approach to data collection and analysis, contributing to quality reporting.

Contribute to accountable emergency WASH programming

  • Contribute to the preparation of terms of reference for monitoring and evaluation exercises and development of research questions and work to ensure implementation of recommendations for improvement.
  • When appropriate and in line with other work priorities be available to participate as an evaluation team member.

Job Duties and Responsibilities (continued)

Contribute to an effective, high-quality IFRC team:

  • Be accountable to the Regional WASH Coordinator by providing regular progress reports on results against objectives.
  • Be a proactive team member fostering a customer service-oriented culture that values proactivity, continuous improvement, innovation, high performance and cost effectiveness.
  • Foster a co-creative environment with colleagues in the Region and with NSs including actors in the relevant external environment.
  • Be responsible for the project management of sections of the regional project portfolio as required.

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent higher education degree.
  • Technical training courses linked to the post.

Experience

  • 6-7 years’ experience in an adequate field
  • Experience in the humanitarian or development sector, with a focus on WASH
  • Demonstrated professional credibility in the sector and experience working in an international or cross-cultural environment.
  • Experience working in a Red Cross or Red Crescent National Society and/or IFRC or ICRC

Knowledge, Skills and Languages

  • Knowledge of WASH and public health and experience in practically applying this knowledge into policy, programmes and positioning
  • Proactive, innovative, willing, and committed to stay and travel in the remote areas to work with poor and vulnerable communities.
  • Programme and project management
  • Results-oriented and demand-driven individual, entrepreneurial, ability to lead in unprecedented and/or ambiguous situations.
  • Demonstrated track record in innovating, contributing to a learning culture, sharing knowledge and new approaches to engaging partners.
  • Professional credibility, able to work effectively at all levels across the organisation
  • Proven good judgment and ability to work with complete integrity and confidentiality
  • Demonstrated core proficiency in (a) digital communication & collaboration, (b) basic digital content creation, (c) digital safety & security, (d) data literacy, and (e) problem solving with technology (including responsible use of AI assistants.
  • Understanding of and commitment to IFRC’s mission and values.

Competencies, Values and Comments

Values: Respect for diversity; Integrity; Professionalism; Accountability

Core competencies: Communication; Collaboration and teamwork; Judgement and decision making; National society and customer relations; Creativity and innovation; Building trust.

The National Federation of Women Living with HIV and AIDS (NFWLHA), was officially registered in 2007 with a vision to create a just and equitable society for women and children infected and affected with HIV, so that they can live a productive, empowered and dignified life, free from stigma and discrimination. Underpinned by guiding principles of gender equity and human rights, evidence-based planning, programming, and policy advocacy, NFWLHA has broadened its strategic intervention areas over the last nine years, focusing mainly on strengthening and capacity development of the network, knowledge management for evidence-based policy advocacy and community system strengthening.

Currently, NFWLHA is implementing the Treatment, Care and Support Program in 25 districts across Koshi, Madhesh, and Bagmati Provinces with support from the Global Fund through UNDP. To support the effective implementation of this program, NFWLHA invites applications from qualified and motivated candidates for the following position:

Position: Finance Assistant-1 (Treatment Care and Support Program)

Duty Station: NFWLHA Central Office, Kathmandu (Frequent travel to program district)

Reports/responsible to: Finance Head and Finance Coordinator

Supervisory Responsibilities: Program cum finance officers

Purpose of the Position:

The Finance Assistant will provide support to the finance department in managing the financial operations of NFWLHA. This will include assisting with accounting tasks, processing payments, maintaining financial records, and ensuring compliance with financial policies and procedures.

Major Responsibilities:

Accounting Support:

  • Assist in day-to-day accounting operations, including data entry, record keeping, and financial transactions.
  • Prepare and process payments to vendors, partners, and staff.
  • Reconcile bank statements and other financial reports.
  • Maintain accurate and organized financial files and records.

Financial Management:

  • Assist in the preparation of budgets and financial reports.
  • Track expenses and monitor budget performance.
  • Support the financial management of projects and programs.
  • Ensure compliance with financial policies, procedures, and donor requirements.

Administrative Support:

  • Provide general administrative and clerical support to the finance department.
  • Assist with the preparation of audit documents and financial statements.
  • Manage petty cash and other financial transactions.

Reporting and recording

  • Maintain all financial records and books of account as per the NFWLHA policy.
  • Prepare a monthly statement of expenditure.
  • Assist the Administration and Finance Manager and Officer in preparing financial statements for the Program Manager, Coordinator, and the Executive Committee.
  • Produce financial information, and budget-monitoring information regularly to help the Administration and Finance Officer, Program Manager, and Coordinator to monitor budgets.

Meeting and communications

  • Participate in meetings to ensure that information is shared with appropriate staff members.
  • Fulfill and participate in finance-related meetings with concerned stakeholders and funding agencies in the absence of administration and finance officers.

Organizational Development

  • Follow NFWLHA’s formulated policies, internal rules and regulations and contribute to the achievement of long-term objectives of the organization.
  • Actively participate in the process of organizational change process and implement Strategic plan directions.

Education and Qualification

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in finance or accounting, preferably in a non-profit organization.
  • Strong knowledge of basic accounting principles and procedures.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other accounting software.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills.
  • Fluency in Nepali and English (written and spoken).
  • Knowledge of HIV/AIDS-related issues, gender equity, and social inclusion (preferred).
  • Preference will be given to candidates with experience in Global Fund projects and working knowledge of FAMOUS, True Books, and Tally accounting software.

To Apply:

Interested and eligible candidates are requested to apply with CV, Reference contact details, Cover letter with expected salary and relevant certificates at nfwlha.vacancy@gmail.com before 25th September, 2026, Friday. Interviews will begin on rolling basis and the best fit candidate will be selected immediately.

NFWLHA recognizes that it has the responsibility to respect and promote gender equality and the safety and protection of all. NFWLHA has a ZERO-tolerance policy regarding abuse. NFWLHA reserves the right of conducting a background check of the potential candidates. Only Shortlisted candidate will be contacted.

Closure Date: 03/Oct/2026, 3:44:00 AM
