FAO seeks gender, geographical and linguistic diversity in order to best serve FAO Members in all regions.

FAO is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, background and culture
Qualified female applicants, qualified nationals of non-and under-represented Members and person with disabilities are encouraged to apply
Everyone who works for FAO is required to adhere to the highest standards of integrity and professional conduct, and to uphold FAO’s values
FAO, as a Specialized Agency of the United Nations, has a zero-tolerance policy for conduct that is incompatible with its status, objectives and mandate, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination
All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference and background checks
All applications will be treated with the strictest confidentiality

Organizational Setting

FAO is a specialized agency of the UN that leads international efforts to defeat hunger. FAO’s goal is to achieve food security for all and ensure that people have regular access to enough high-quality food to lead active, healthy lives. With 195 Members (194 countries and the European Union), FAO works in over 130 countries worldwide.

FAO Country Offices, working under overall corporate guidance and in line with the Strategic Framework, offer policy advice and support to countries in the mandated areas of FAO, facilitated through partnerships, resources and an active country programme to provide technical assistance, develop capacities and deliver core services while fully observing international standards of accountability to establish leadership and strengthen impact at the country level.

The offices deliver on the programmatic priorities of each country as agreed in their respective Country Programming Frameworks (CPFs) aligned to the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) and ensure effective and efficient operations with adequate human and financial resources.

Specifically, FAO Country Offices:

  • advocate, inform and support policies and investments in the areas of FAO’s mandate;
  •  provide technical assistance and deliver core services;
  •  assist and catalyse partnership and resource mobilization activities to support agrifood systems transformation;
  • Position FAO as the specialized/authoritative technical agency in food and agriculture and agrifood systems transformation;
  • ensure risk-smart and accountable operations and management.

Despite being continuously dependent on agriculture, with 67 percent of the population living in agricultural households, Nepal’s agriculture sector still struggles with low productivity, limited competitiveness, and weak commercialization. These challenges have severely limited income-generation opportunities and broader rural transformation efforts, further contributing to the persistent outmigration of youth and the deterioration of the long-term vitality of farming communities. Women, in this context, carry multiple responsibilities and obligations while lacking access to productive resources, services, technologies and decision-making spaces. Meanwhile, Nepal’s agrifood systems are becoming increasingly vulnerable to growing climate-related shocks and stresses. The resilience of smallholder farmers and local food systems is becoming increasingly fragile under these compounding pressures. Adding to these challenges are food and nutrition insecurity, limited access to clean and safe drinking water, and the absence of sustainable long-term operation and maintenance systems, highlighting the need for integrated and locally grounded intervention.

As a result of these challenges, FAO Nepal has been requested by the Government of Nepal, represented by the Ministry of Agriculture, Forest and Environment, to provide technical assistance for the project “Strengthening Agrifood System in Nepal” under the Global Development and South-South Cooperation Fund supported through CIDCA. The project is designed as a 24-month initiative with a total budget of USD 2,488,810. The implementation will focus on Nepal’s hill and mountain regions, with Mandandeupur Municipality and Panchkhal Municipality in Kavre and Rong Rural Municipality and Suryodaya Municipality in Ilam serving as demonstration sites for piloting and operationalizing the interventions.The projects aim to strengthen the foundation for long-term agrifood systems transformation in Nepal through comprehensive interventions that emphasize governance capacity, scaling up climate-smart and nutrition-sensitive technologies, improving market access and inclusion, expanding water security solutions, and promoting environmental sustainability and agrobiodiversity conservation. Institutional strengthening, alongside field-level investments and community-based actions, will also be prioritized to secure stronger support from local governments, farmer organizations, and partner institutions.

To support effective project delivery and ensure quality implementation, FAO Nepal seeks to engage two Field Facilitation Supports, one based in Kavrepalanchok District, and one based in Ilam District, to provide day-to-day field facilitation support and technical support for project implementation. The Field Facilitation Support in Kavrepalanchok will support activities in Mandandeupur Municipality and Panchkhal Municipality, while the Field Facilitation Support in Ilam will support activities in the designated municipalities under the guidance and supervision of FAO personnel. Their responsibilities will include supporting field implementation, beneficiary registration, data collection, monitoring, documentation, reporting, and logistical arrangements for project activities, in accordance with approved workplans and FAO procedures.

Reporting Lines

The Field Facilitation Support will work under the overall supervision of the Assistant FAO Representative (Programme) in Nepal, Programme Manager and the direct supervision of the Project Coordinator for the project “Strengthening Agrifood Systems in Nepal” (GCP/NEP/094/CPR).

Technical Focus

The Field Facilitation Support will provide technical and operational support to project implementation, monitoring, data collection, documentation and reporting activities at the municipal level under the direct supervision of FAO technical personnel. The Field Facilitation Support will support field-level activities related to climate-smart and nutrition-sensitive agriculture, agrifood systems development, beneficiary engagement, capacity-development events, monitoring activities and project documentation.

Tasks and responsibilities

  • Assist the FAO Supervisor in preparing municipality-level implementation schedules and activity plans based on approved project workplans.
  • Support transparent beneficiary identification, verification and mobilization, ensuring inclusion targets and disaggregated records are maintained.
  •  Support baseline surveys, field assessments, value chain assessments, data collection exercises and compilation of project-related information as directed by the FAO Supervisor.
  •  Assist in organizing trainings, demonstrations, farmer field activities, nutrition field activities, awareness campaigns, consultations and exchange visits, including logistical and administrative arrangements.
  • Support the dissemination of technical information and training materials related to climate-smart agriculture, nutrition-sensitive agriculture, agroecological practices, soil fertility management, integrated pest management, water-use efficiency and food safety under the guidance of FAO technical personnel.
  •  Support producer groups, cooperatives and enterprises participating in project activities by maintaining records and facilitating their participation in project interventions.
  • Assist in site verification, distribution tracking, installation support, user orientation and monitoring of project-supported inputs, equipment, irrigation systems, storage facilities and other assets.
  • Support the collection and maintenance of records related to project-supported infrastructure, equipment and community-level interventions.
  •  Maintain municipality-level project documentation, including attendance records, participant profiles, photographs, geotagged information, field visit notes, evaluation forms, distribution records and beneficiary feedback.
  • Collect, compile and submit progress information, supporting documentation and evidence related to project outputs and indicators.
  •  Assist in documenting field observations, achievements, challenges, lessons learned, success stories and beneficiary experiences for reporting purposes.
  •  Support monitoring visits undertaken by FAO personnel and promptly report observations and issues to the FAO Supervisor for follow-up.
  •  Assist FAO personnel in organizing meetings, workshops, field visits, assessments and review events at municipal level.
  • Provide logistical and administrative support for field missions, monitoring visits, assessments and project-related events.
  •  Assist in the preparation of reports, presentations, briefing materials and other project documentation by compiling relevant data and supporting information.
  • Apply gender equality, social inclusion, environmental sustainability, climate resilience, safeguarding, informed consent, confidentiality, responsible data management and do-no-harm principles while carrying out assigned duties.

CANDIDATES WILL BE ASSESSED AGAINST THE FOLLOWING

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Agriculture, Agricultural Economics, Rural Development, Natural Resource Management, Development Studies or a related field.
  • At least five years of relevant experience in agriculture, rural development, food security, climate resilience or community-based projects.
  •  Working knowledge of English and Nepali.
  • National of Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal or resident of the country with a valid work permit.

FAO Core Competencies

  • Results Focus
  •  Teamwork
  • Communication
  • Building Effective Relationships
  • Knowledge Sharing and Continuous Improvement

Technical/Functional Skills

  •  Experience working with local governments, farmer groups, cooperatives, women’s groups and community organizations.
  • Proven experience in field-level project implementation, training, beneficiary mobilization, monitoring, reporting and stakeholder coordination.
  •  Good understanding of agrifood systems, value chains, climate-smart agriculture, nutrition-sensitive agriculture and rural livelihoods.
  •  Experience in data collection, documentation, monitoring and evaluation, and report preparation.
  • Strong communication, facilitation, coordination and problem-solving skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and digital data-collection and reporting tools.
  • Ability to work effectively in multicultural environments and undertake frequent field travel.

Selection Criteria

  •  Extent and relevance of experience in municipality-level agricultural or rural-development project implementation.
  •  Extent and relevance of experience in training, demonstrations, community engagement and stakeholder coordination.
  • Knowledge of local government systems, Agriculture Knowledge Centres and community institutions.
  •  Experience with development partners, NGOs, United Nations agencies or government programmes.
  •  Understanding of gender equality, social inclusion, environmental sustainability and safeguarding principles.
  •  Working knowledge of Chinese is an asset for coordination with Chinese experts and institutions under the CIDCA-supported project.

Please note that all candidates should adhere to FAO Values of Commitment to FAO, Respect for All and Integrity and Transparency.

FAO’s commitment to environmental sustainability is integral to our strategic objectives and operations.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

  • FAO does not charge a fee at any stage of the recruitment process (application, interview meeting, processing).
  • Applications received after the closing date will not be accepted.
  • Please note that FAO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU) / United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). The list can be accessed at http://www.whed.net/
  • For other issues, visit the FAO employment website: http://www.fao.org/employment/home/en/
  • Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, and security clearances. Subject to certain exemptions, vaccination against COVID-19 will in principle be required. Vaccination status will be verified as part of the medical clearance process.

HOW TO APPLY

  • To apply, visit the recruitment website at Jobs at FAO and complete your online profile. We strongly recommend that your profile is accurate, complete and includes your employment records, academic qualifications, and language skills
  •  Candidates are requested to attach a letter of motivation to the online profile
  •  Once your profile is completed, please apply, and submit your application
  • Please note that FAO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU) / United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). The list can be accessed at http://www.whed.net/. These qualifications should be in alignment with the International Standard Classification of Education (ISCED) mappings.
  • Candidates may be requested to provide performance assessments and authorization to conduct verification checks of past and present work, character, education, military and police records to ascertain any and all information which may be pertinent to the employment qualifications
  •  Incomplete applications will not be considered
  •  Personal information provided on your application may be shared within FAO and with other companies acting on FAO’s behalf to provide employment support services such as pre-screening of applications, assessment tests, background checks and other related services. You will be asked to provide your consent before submitting your application. You may withdraw consent at any time, by withdrawing your application, in such case FAO will no longer be able to consider your application
  • Only applications received through the FAO recruitment portal will be considered
  •  Your application will be screened based on the information provided in your online profile
  •  We encourage applicants to submit the application well before the deadline date.

If you need help or have queries, please create a one-time registration with FAO’s client support team for further assistance: https://fao.service-now.com/csp

With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type:

Local – Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

WVI Nepal has declared a Category II National Response and is implementing one-year multi-sectoral humanitarian response and recovery focused on food, nutrition, shelter, education WASH, livelihood and protection services for affected families. To support approximately 5,000 affected households in reaching an estimate of approximately 25,000 people, the target and timeline can be increased based on the fund and evolving needs of the affected people.

The District Coordinator will lead and coordinate the implementation of the Nepal flash flood response project at Rasuwa district and municipal levels. The position is responsible for ensuring timely, quality, and accountable delivery of humanitarian assistance and early recovery interventions, maintaining strong coordination with local government and stakeholders, and achieving project targets in line with organizational and donor requirements. Additionally, this position will represent WVI Nepal in the district as required and oversee the local partner NGO’s performance, compliances (security, safeguarding, financial, procurement), assurance quality, and participate in partner NGO’s meeting (including Board meeting) to provide and get updates as well.

The incumbent should be a team player, agile and strategic leader, issue and problem solving and emphatic. The role expects to maintain a good rapport and coordination with peer organizations, key stakeholders including the government line agencies.

This position is expected to have a comprehensive understanding and operational skill to expedite the momentum of the programme delivery. This includes creating an enabling and conducive environment in the given working areas of the district.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Project implementation yielding envisioned results

  • Lead the day-to-day implementation of project activities across all sectors as per the response plan and agreed budget
  • Ensure activities are implemented according to approved plans, budgets, timelines, and quality standards.
  • Support municipal and community level planning and implementation processes.
  • Monitor project progress and identify implementation challenges and solutions.
  • Ensure integration of protection, gender, inclusion, safeguarding, and accountability principles throughout project activities.
  • Frequent travel to working municipalities and monitor progress and coordination with the local governments.

Stakeholder Engagement and Representation to profile and collaborate on given themes or scope

  • Build relationships with district and local governments, community stakeholders, implementing partner NGOs and other INGOs/NGOs in coordination with project team and relevant staff from National Office.
  • Represent the organization in district and local level coordination meetings.
  • Strengthen collaboration with community leaders, local partners, and community-based organizations.
  • Facilitate joint monitoring visits and review meetings with stakeholders.

Monitoring, Reporting and Accountability to ensure quality and compliance intact

  • Track project achievements against indicators and targets.
  • Prepare monthly reports, and other reports as required, for the Response Operations, working with District staff as needed
  • Ensure timely collection, verification, and submission of project data and reports.
  • Support assessments, monitoring visits, and evaluations.
  • Ensure community feedback and complaints mechanisms are functioning effectively and concerns are addressed promptly.
  • Document lessons learned to accompany the performance reports.
  • Provide report to the local government as requested/required

Partner NGO Management to implement effectively and efficiently

  • Provide guidance and support to the NGO partners to deliver quality result
  • Conduct regular review and periodic appraisals of NGO partners to build their capacities, in line with MOUs
  • Ensure the staff and board members of the NGO partners align with WVIN’s policies and requirements
  • Support NGO partners to undertake procurement in line with WV NGO partner procurement policy

Financial and Resource Management

  • Monitor project expenditures and budget utilization.
  • Review activity plans and forecasts for efficient resource allocation.
  • Ensure compliance with donor and organizational financial procedures.
  • Support on budget reviews and development of business plans.
  • Find avenues to be more effective and efficient.

Risk Management and Safeguarding

  • Identify programmatic, operational, and security risks and propose mitigation measures.
  • Ensure adult and child safeguarding, child protection, and code of conduct standards are understood and applied.
  • Report incidents and concerns through established organizational procedures.

KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE

Required Education, training, license, registration and certification

  • Bachelor’s degree in Disaster Management, Rural Development, Social Sciences, Development Studies, or related field.

Required Professional Experience

  • Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in humanitarian response, early recovery disaster management, or development programming.
  • At least 2 years of experience managing field-based projects and teams.
  • Experience in emergency response and coordination with government structures.

Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications

  • Timely achievement of project targets and milestones.
  • Quality and timeliness of donor and internal reports.
  • Effective coordination with local government and stakeholders.
  • Budget utilization within approved limits.
  • Compliance with safeguarding, accountability, and quality standards.
  • Community satisfaction and effective response to feedback and complaints.

Work Base: Rasuwa District

Duration: One year

Travel and/or Work Environment

Willingness to work outside office hours, especially when conducting monitoring/field visits, when hosting donor visits, and when meeting.

Physical Requirements

Will be required to spend at least 50% of work time conducting monitoring and field visits in target municipalities and wards

Language Requirements

  • Effective written and oral communication skills, including presentation and reporting skills (both English and Nepali).
  • Knowledge of local language and culture is a value add.

WVI Nepal has zero tolerance to child rights’ violations, by employees and/or affiliates.”

Posiiton: MEAL Coordinator
Location: Kathmandu, Nepal
End Date: September 27, 2026

With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type:

Local – Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

World Vision International Nepal (WVI Nepal) has launched a Category II Emergency Response in the priority districts of Rasuwa and Nuwakot, Bagmati Province, following devastating flash floods along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors that caused casualties, displacement, and extensive damage across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. The 12-month Nepal Flash Flood Response (NFFR) 2026 plan targets 25,000 people, including 10,000 children, from around 5,000 affected households across seven sectors, moving from relief into early recovery.

This position has responsibility to lead the monitoring evaluation accountability and learning (MEAL) function of the Nepal Flash Flood Response project to support to functionalize MEAL system and processes with focus on key priorities like assessment, survey, monitoring, community feedback response mechanism, evaluation, learning documentation, information/evidence collection, beneficiary tracking, and reporting for the project. The position is further designed to support development and operationalization of the manual and digital system/platform for the project that contributes knowledge management and reporting expectations. This position will support the integrated knowledge management position based in the national office. The work further includes coordination, network, and collaboration with the project team and stakeholders, which are effective to meet the efficient MEAL standards and practices.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Assessment and evaluation studies

  • Technically prepare, guide, and implement any assessment (including needs assessment) or evaluation work related to the project in collaboration with the implementing partners.
  • Develop, adapt, and finalize the required number and types of tools, digital systems, and guidelines for assessments and evaluation when needed.
  • Analyze (self or with consultant) the assessment/evaluation data and share the assessment findings in agreed format and structure.
  • Technically support sharing the findings with relevant stakeholders and people using best appropriate means and methods.
  • Ensuring timely dissemination of assessment and evaluation findings to relevant stakeholders, including donors and government authorities (local, provincial, and federal), in line with agreed plans and requirements.

Monitoring, accountability, and learning

  • Under the guidance of Project Manager/Coordinator and NO MEAL team, develop and implement quality monitoring systems (including quality standards and digital tools) for the project activities.
  • Regularly review and analyze project progress data (using SharePoint, CommCare and PBI Dashboard) to identify from information management systems gaps, inform decision-making, and recommend corrective actions.
  • Lead and/or participate in monitoring visits to communities, institutions, and stakeholders to verify outputs and ensure quality programming.
  • Ensure monitoring findings are properly documented, communicated, and followed by agreed action plans, with consistent follow-up until issues are resolved.
  • Plan and manage post-distribution monitoring (PDMs) following assistance to disaster-affected populations.
  • Provide technical guidance and oversight (to the project team) in beneficiary selection and verification processes to ensure transparency, adherence to criteria, and accountable programming practices.
  • Prepare and share PDM reports with project teams, support offices, and donors to inform improvement actions.
  • Conduct qualitative outcome monitoring in line with project timelines, including data collection, analysis, and documentation of evidence to report against project objectives and indicators.

Organizational Setting

FAO is a specialized agency of the UN that leads international efforts to defeat hunger. FAO’s goal is to achieve food security for all and ensure that people have regular access to enough high-quality food to lead active, healthy lives. With 195 Members (194 countries and the European Union), FAO works in over 130 countries worldwide.

FAO Country Offices, working under overall corporate guidance and in line with the Strategic Framework, offer policy advice and support to countries in the mandated areas of FAO, facilitated through partnerships, resources and an active country programme to provide technical assistance, develop capacities and deliver core services while fully observing international standards of accountability to establish leadership and strengthen impact at the country level.

The offices deliver on the programmatic priorities of each country as agreed in their respective Country Programming Frameworks (CPFs) aligned to the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) and ensure effective and efficient operations with adequate human and financial resources.

Specifically, FAO Country Offices:

(i) advocate, inform and support policies and investments in the areas of FAO’s mandate;
(ii) provide technical assistance and deliver core services;
(iii) assist and catalyse partnership and resource mobilization activities to support agrifood systems transformation;
(iv) Position FAO as the specialized/authoritative technical agency in food and agriculture and agrifood systems transformation;
(v) ensure risk-smart and accountable operations and management.

Nepal’s agrifood systems continue to face significant challenges, including low agricultural productivity, weak commercialization, climate vulnerability, food and nutrition insecurity, limited access to safe drinking water, and inadequate operation and maintenance systems. These constraints disproportionately affect smallholder farmers, women, and rural communities, limiting livelihood opportunities and contributing to youth outmigration.

To address these challenges, FAO Nepal, at the request of the Government of Nepal, is implementing the project “Strengthening Agrifood Systems in Nepal” (GCP/NEP/094/CPR) under the Global Development and South-South Cooperation Fund supported by the China International Development Cooperation Agency (CIDCA). The 24-month project, with a budget of USD 2.49 million, supports agrifood systems transformation in Kavre and Ilam districts through interventions on governance, production, nutrition, enterprise development, water systems, social inclusion, and environmental sustainability.

In parallel, FAO Nepal is implementing the UN Joint Programme “Innovative Financial Solutions for Local Food Systems Transformation in Nepal” (UNJP/NEP/091/UNJ), funded by the Joint SDG Fund and jointly implemented with UNDP, WFP, and UNCDF. Under this programme, FAO leads the development of innovative financing solutions, including blended finance, public-private partnerships (PPPs), investment pipeline development, and support to women-led agribusinesses and cooperatives in Panchkhal Municipality.

Given the strong complementarities between the CIDCA-supported project and the Joint SDG Fund programme, particularly in Panchkhal Municipality, coordinated implementation is essential to maximize synergies, strengthen stakeholder engagement, avoid duplication, and enhance the sustainability and impact of project investments.

To support effective implementation, FAO Nepal seeks a National Project Coordinator.

The National Project Coordinator will be under the overall supervision of the Assistant FAOR (Programme), and the direct supervision of the Programme Manager and relevant FAO technical officers.

ITC’s mission is to foster inclusive and sustainable economic growth through trade and international business development. Through its projects and programmes, ITC contributes to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and advances the global Aid for Trade agenda. ITC is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland (www.intracen.org). ITC is seeking an Associate Monitoring and Evaluation Expert for the Trade Facilitation Programme for South Asia, a four-year regional programme implemented by ITC and funded by the European Union. The programme covers Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka and aims to strengthen the capacity of institutions and businesses across South Asia to better understand, utilise and comply with requirements governing access to the European Union market. The overall objective of the programme is to leverage trade as a driver of sustainable development, poverty reduction and more inclusive socio-economic outcomes. Its specific objective is to enhance the readiness of South Asian institutions and SMEs to understand, utilise and comply with EU market-access requirements. It will also promote regional and country-level cooperation, contribute to business linkages and more sustainable and resilient value chains between South Asia and the European Union. Duties and Responsibilities

BACKGROUND:

The International Trade Centre (ITC) is the joint agency of the World Trade Organization (WTO) and the United Nations (UN). It is the only multilateral organization fully dedicated to supporting the internationalization and competitiveness of small, and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). ITC’s mission is to foster inclusive and sustainable economic growth through trade and international business development. Through its projects and programmes, ITC contributes to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and advances the global Aid for Trade agenda. ITC is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland (www.intracen.org). ITC is seeking a Project Assistant for the Trade Facilitation Programme for South Asia, a four-year regional programme implemented by ITC and funded by the European Union. The programme covers Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka and aims to strengthen the capacity of institutions and businesses across South Asia to better understand, utilise and comply with requirements governing access to the European Union market. The overall objective of the programme is to leverage trade as a driver of sustainable development, poverty reduction and more inclusive socio-economic outcomes. Its specific objective is to enhance the readiness of South Asian institutions and SMEs to understand, utilise and comply with EU market-access requirements. The programme is structured around three key Outputs:

  •  Output 1: Strengthened capacity to interpret and effectively utilise EU preferential trading arrangements, including Everything But Arms (EBA), the Generalised Scheme of Preferences (GSP) and GSP+.
  •  Output 2: Enhanced preparedness to comply with EU environmental sustainability-related trade legislation and requirements, including those linked to the European Green Deal.
  • Output 3: Strengthened awareness and capacities to address EU legislation and standards related to corporate sustainability due diligence, labour rights and gender equality.

Through these interventions, the programme will support public institutions, business support organisations and private-sector actors in priority sectors and value chains to strengthen regulatory readiness, improve market-access capabilities and respond to evolving EU sustainability and due-diligence requirements. It will also promote regional and country-level cooperation, contribute to business linkages and more sustainable and resilient value chains between South Asia and the European Union. The position is located within ITC’s Office for Asia and the Pacific (OAP). The Project Assistant will be based in the programme office in Kathmandu, Nepal, and will provide administrative, logistical and programme support to the Regional Team Leader and the wider project team, ensuring the efficient day-to-day functioning of the programme office and implementation of project activities.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Under the overall guidance of the Project Manager of OAP, based in Geneva, Switzerland, and the direct supervision of the Regional Team Leader, the Project Assistant will be responsible for performing the following duties:
  •  Assists in the coordination of project planning and preparation work for, typically, a medium-size and complex component of the project initiatives; monitors status of project proposals and receipt of relevant documentation for review and approval.
  • Compiles, summarizes, and presents basic information/data on specific project and related topics or issues.
  • Reviews project documents, especially cost plans/budgets, for completeness and compliance with relevant rules and procedures prior to submission for final approval and signature; identifies inconsistencies; distributes project documents to relevant parties upon approval.
  • Reviews budget revisions; verifies availability of funds; ensures necessary approval and entry in computerized budget system.
  • Serves as focal point for administrative coordination of project implementation activities, involving extensive liaison with diverse organizational units to initiate requests, obtain necessary clearances, process and follow-up on administrative actions, e.g. travel arrangements, training/study tours, authorization of payments, disbursement of funds, procurement of equipment and services, etc.
  • Compiles, summarizes and enters data on project delivery; drafts related status reports, identifying shortfalls in delivery, budget overruns, etc., and brings to the attention of management.
  • Drafts correspondence on budget-related issues and prepares and updates periodic reports, briefing notes, graphic and statistical summaries, accounting spreadsheets, etc.
  • Provides general office assistance; responds to complex information requests and inquiries; reviews, logs and routes incoming correspondence; sets up and maintains files/records; organizes meetings, workshops; handles routine administrative tasks, such as maintaining attendance records, assessing telephone billing, etc.
  • Performs other duties as assigned. COMPETENCIES:

Knowledge of internal policies, processes and procedures generally and in particular those related to programme/project administration, implementation and evaluation, technical cooperation, programming and budgeting. Understanding of the functions and organization of the work unit and of the organizational structure and respective roles of related units. As a global leader, CARE is shaping the future of the humanitarian and development sector. Each year, we deliver support and services to millions of people in over a hundred countries. We do this by focusing on our mission and living the values that drive our organization. A career at CARE is an opportunity to be part of a movement that brings communities together to solve complex problems and foster lasting change throughout the world. We seek individuals who are passionate about humanitarian and development work, collaborate well with others, embrace learning and innovation, and deliver results.

CARE has been operational in Nepal since 1978 and works in partnerships with government and non-government stakeholders across the spectrum of humanitarian action and long-term development programs. We create local solutions to poverty and inequality and seek dignity for everyone every day and during times of crisis. CARE puts women and girls at the center of everything we do because they have proven to be the best hope for creating lasting change in the world.

What it’s like to work at CARE?

CARE is a mission-driven international humanitarian aid and development organization that offers an opportunity to work with people across the world. Not a day will go by that you won’t learn something profound, meet an expert, or write a sentence that can change a life. We are committed to an environment where everyone can succeed.

The Nurture Every Future- Poshan is being implemented in Sudurpaschim, Karnali, Lumbini, and Madhesh Provinces, targeting nine districts with high rates of malnutrition and poor health and nutrition outcomes. The Nurture Every Future – Poshan aims to improve the wellbeing of children and their mothers in targeted districts of Nepal. The interventions aim to strengthen the capacity for health and nutrition services, improve care and feeding practices; increase household food security; promote food safety and hygiene; and promote women’s empowerment and leadership.

CARE Nepal hereby invites applications, for the below mentioned positions for (Nurture Every Future- Poshan, from interested Nepalese candidates.

Finance and Sub Grant Officer (Nurture Every Future- Poshan) based in Madhesh Province
The Finance and Sub-Grant Officer will be responsible for ensuring effective financial management, compliance, and oversight of sub-grants in accordance with organizational policies, donor regulations, and statutory requirements. The position supports the planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, and financial reporting of sub-grants while ensuring that project expenditures are aligned with approved budgets and grant agreements.

The role strengthens partners’ financial management capacity through regular coaching, financial reviews, compliance monitoring, and technical support, while ensuring timely resolution of identified gaps and promoting accountability and sound stewardship of project resources. The incumbent will coordinate with program and finance teams to facilitate timely fund disbursements, budget revisions, liquidation processing, and accurate financial record-keeping to support efficient project implementation. In addition, the incumbent is responsible for processing accounting transactions related to CARE offices and staff, ensuring compliance with internal controls and financial procedures. The employee is expected to fully comply with CARE’s safety and security policies and remain accountable for their implementation

The employee shall fully comply with CARE policies and procedures and should be accountable for it.

Posiiton: Administrative Assistant
Vacancy No.: S18628
Category of Contract: National
Position Type: National
Application Deadline: 25/09/2026
Job Posted On: 18/09/2026
Duty Station: Kathmandu
Country: NEPAL
Grade: National Staff
Duty Station Status: N/A
Accompanied Status: N/A
Duration: 12 months

Organizational Context

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe. The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. The IFRC is currently present in Nepal through a Country Delegation (CD – first established in 1965 with a presence through regional representation at times), providing support to Nepal Red Cross Society (NRCS) programmes and National Society development (NSD) amongst as well as emergency response, other areas. The longer-term mission of the Nepal Delegation is to facilitate organisational growth, technical capacities, partnerships, and resource mobilisation that enable Nepal Red Cross Society to deliver on its humanitarian mandate in the country through the provision of technical support, advocacy, representation and coordination functions, in accordance with Strategy 2030, the IFRC Renewal and annual Operational Plans. The Country Delegation also provides integration services to six IFRC members with a presence in Nepal. On 26 August 2026, a major ice-rock avalanche occurred in the upper Bhote Koshi watershed near the China–Nepal border, resulting in an historically powerful flash flood that advanced from the border down the entire length of Nepal along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli River basins. Due to the evolving operational requirements of the Rasuwa Flash Flood 2026 response operation, this role profile provides an overview of the principal responsibilities and functions associated with this position within a Federation-coordinated operation.

Job Purpose: This position caters to the daily administrative operations of the Country Delegation Nepal of IFRC, especially to the office and administrative needs of the PNSs which are under operation.

Job Duties and Responsibilities

  •  Support the efficient implementation of office administrative procedures and workflows.
  • Coordinate administrative support services for staff, delegates, visitors, and partner National Societies as required.
  •  Maintain and update filing systems, databases, contact lists, inventories, contracts, agreements, and administrative records in both electronic and hard-copy formats.
  •  Assist in preparing correspondence, reports, meeting minutes, presentations, and other administrative documents.
  • Coordinate domestic travel arrangements, including air ticket bookings, hotel reservations, and maintenance of travel-related records. Liaise with the fleet team to arrange and track airport pick-up and drop-off services for visitors as required.
  •  Assist in arranging residential accommodation for delegates, including sourcing suitable housing options, coordinating property viewings, preparing inventory documentation, liaising with landlords, and facilitating administrative processes related to lease agreements and utility services.
  • Provide administrative support for domestic meetings, workshops, trainings, conferences, field visits, and official events across Nepal, including venue arrangements, accommodation, transportation, participant coordination, and other event-related requirements.
  •  Support procurement processes in accordance with IFRC policies and procedures, including obtaining quotations, preparing procurement documentation, following up on deliveries, maintaining procurement records, and processing administrative invoices and supporting documentation.
  • Track and process telecommunication, internet, utility, and other administrative service bills, ensuring timely payments and compliance with IFRC policies and procedures.

Job Duties and Responsibilities (continued)

  •  Maintain updated inventory and asset registers and support periodic physical verification of office assets.
  •  Monitor office supplies and stationery stocks and arrange timely replenishment.
  • Liaise with vendors, landlords, service providers, and maintenance contractors to ensure timely and quality service delivery.
  • Support management of office facilities, utilities, office equipment, and maintenance requirements.
  •  Monitor administrative service agreements and contracts and coordinate timely renewals when required.
  • Ensure proper documentation, filing, and archiving of administrative records and correspondence.
  •  Maintain confidentiality of sensitive organizational information and records.
  • Support compliance with administrative policies, procedures, and operational standards.
  • Be proactive and liaise with different department to ensure the smooth functioning of Administration Unit and delivery of services in an efficient and effective manner.

Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent higher education degree.

Experience

Required: 2-3 years’ experience in a relevant field Proactive, innovative, willing, and committed to staying and traveling in remote areas to work with vulnerable communities. Preferred: Experience in working in an international environment, preferably with the United Nations or a similar organization Experience within the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement

Knowledge, Skills and Languages

Excellent professional communication skills, both verbal and written in both English and Nepali A high degree of competence in teamwork, commitment to the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement and its work, integrity and personal conduct, flexibility and adaptability Sound knowledge of Microsoft Office applications Demonstrated core proficiency in (a) digital communication & collaboration, (b) basic digital content creation, (c) digital safety & security, (d) data literacy, and (e) problem solving with technology (including responsible use of AI assistants. Understanding of and commitment to IFRC’s mission and values.

Competencies, Values and Comments

Values: Respect for diversity; Integrity; Professionalism; Accountability Core competencies: Communication; Collaboration and teamwork; Judgement and decision making; National society and customer relations; Creativity and innovation; Building trust

Posiiton: WASH & Shelter Coordinator
Location: Kathmandu

End Date: September 27, 2026

With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type:

Local – Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

World Vision International Nepal (WVI Nepal) has launched a Category II Emergency Response in the priority districts of Rasuwa and Nuwakot, Bagmati Province, following devastating flash floods along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors that caused casualties, displacement and extensive damage across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. The 12-month Nepal Flash Flood Response (NFFR) 2026 plan targets 25,000 people, including 10,000 children, from around 5,000 affected households across seven sectors, moving from relief into early recovery.

The WASH & Shelter Coordinator will provide overall planning, technical leadership and oversight for the WASH and Shelter interventions under the Nepal Flash Flood Response 2026 related projects in Rasuwa and Nuwakot district. WASH coordinator’s main responsibility will be planning, assessment, design, development estimate costing, providing overall quality oversight of the physical infrastructure construction/rehabilitation of WASH facilities, Shelter etc. including facilitation of the soft components – awareness, social mobilization and ensuring the standards of the WASH and Shelter technical parts of projects planned in the projects as well. This position will have regular coordination among internal teams for the required technical input, with Partner NGOs and all relevant stakeholders.

This position will lead technical input, field implementation, coordination with partner non-government organizations & government stakeholders, participation in the cluster meeting at local/district level, reporting and support required technical documents as per the government standard and norms.

This role envisions a good team player, managing issues and problem solving, innovative and agile leadership. Overall purpose of this role is to ensure the planned activities are timely delivered to the targeted populace, and key learnings are captured for future interventions.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Project implementation and technical support engagement

  • Identify and implement the appropriate technologies used in WASH and Shelter programs which are culturally appropriate, user friendly and safe for environment
  • Coordinate and mobilize communities and local partners on WASH and Infrastructure activity planning, designing and implementation.
  • Facilitate needs assessment, problem identification, stakeholder and situation analysis along with project team in Partner NGO.
  • Provide technical lead regarding design, construction, structural assessment and recommendation for the infrastructure (WASH facilities and Shelter) rehabilitation/construction as per the different phases of responses.
  • Ensure the intervened structures are earthquake resilient, gender and disability friendly.
  • Provide technical backstopping in preparing construction material specifications, monitoring construction quality, and estimating quantities and costs of materials, equipment, and labor for effective project planning and implementation
  • Coordinate with supply chain management team for required sourcing of the infrastructure facilities and engage in technical evaluation process. Coordinate and contribute for water quality and hygiene maintenance in shelters, and in communities along with health and nutrition team.
  • Train local partners on SPHERE standards and project monitoring for the Infrastructure & WASH interventions.
  • Prepare day-to-day monitoring report.
  • Work closely with Operation Manager for budget preparation and implementation, forecast, support Partner NGOs for the WASH and Shelter related interventions
  • Verify program data through spot checks, field observations, and review of partner reporting systems.
  • Any immediate changes or contextual alteration should be identified and planned ensuring all the given processes

Meet quality of infrastructure activities and ensure timely implementation

  • Conduct regular monitoring, onsite coaching & mentoring and evaluation of all infrastructure construction works within project areas.
  • Ensure timely response and resolutions to the feedback/issues.
  • Coordination with related line agencies/stakeholders at the project locations for smooth operation of construction works.
  • Ensure project on-time delivery, operation & maintenance plans, project quality, and adherence to safety protocols and ensure works are carried out to the appropriate National or International Building Standards.
  • Ensure that construction expenses are made by the phased budget, project budget and compliance with World Vision financial procedure
  • Ensure effective and efficient utilization of program resources through monitoring and tracking expenditures against project plan. Lead budget revision if needed.
  • Maintain a tracker for all infrastructure interventions and proactively plan and implement measures to address and minimize project delays.
  • Construction expenses are in line with budget and World Vision financial procedure.
  • Prepare/Review running bills/completion reports and recommendation for the payment process.
  • Monitor project performance against approved indicators, benchmarks, work plans, and donor requirements.
  • Work closely with the MEAL team to strengthen community feedback and accountability mechanisms and ensure appropriate response to beneficiary concerns.
  • Promote utilization of monitoring and learning findings for adaptive program management.

Networking and Advocacy

  • Represent World Vision in WASH, Shelter cluster and technical working group at district and provincial level.
  • Coordinate with line agencies to plan and implement the Infrastructure & WASH interventions as per the cluster guidance and to address the contextual need.
  • Strengthen relationships with project stakeholders such as Community groups, Children, parents, the Government of Nepal Offices, NGOs, like minded organization and private sectors such as vendors, and contractors to collaboration and avoid the duplication through partnership and cooperation. The Stakeholders assisted with different programs according to the project design.

Timely and quality documentation and reporting

  • Regular update sharing with project teams for the Infrastructure and WASH interventions deliverables.
  • Preparation of certificate of completion for the completed scheme.
  • Prepare operations and maintenance (O & M) manuals for the implemented construction scheme.
  • Document relevant data and evidence to showcase the outcomes of the project
  • Gather photographs and videos of project deliverables, locations, institutions, communities, children, and community members along with stories to share with the wider audience.
  • Support partners in maintaining adequate documentation and evidence required for audits, donor reviews, and compliance assessments
  • Strengthen accountability, transparency, safeguarding, and ethical practices throughout program implementation.
  • Develop quality reports & submit them on time. The reports are expected to showcase impacts to the beneficiaries.
  • Prepare or present progress and completion reports.
  • Support to line manager to prepare monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and annual report in accordance with project compliance.
  • All reports and records are properly documented

KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE

Required Professional Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering with 5 years of experience in WASH, building construction, and disaster-resilient infrastructures.
  • Oral and written communication skills in English and Nepali.
  • Ability to work in a team and be a great team player.
  • Technical knowledge to do construction activities, field surveys, design, drawing & estimation.
  • Technical knowledge to do and check vulnerability assessments of structures.
  • Through understanding of construction works through a community/contractor approach, handling of multiple contractors/UC in NGOs/INGOs.
  • Ability to ensure specification of construction materials/works & ensure the quality of construction works.

Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification

  • Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering or equivalent from the recognized university.
  • Technical knowledge of civil engineering, building construction, and construction contract management in remote locations.
  • Ability to train non-technical users in the use of technical systems in a cross-cultural setting.

Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications

  • Experience in WASH in an emergency context
  • Cross-cultural sensitivity, flexible worldview, emotional maturity, and physical stamina
  • Ability to exhibit an exemplary lifestyle as interpreted in a specific local culture context
  • Team building, collaboration, facilitation and leadership skills
  • Demonstrated networking, partnership and coordination ability
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and detail orientation
  • Able to work under pressure
  • Demonstrate understanding of and commitment to World Vision’s Core Values in the approach to work and relationships
  • Willingness to work outside office hours especially when traveling and working with partners and communities.
  • Skilled in MS Office applications and AUTO CAD

Work Base: Nuwakot District
Duration: One year

Travel and/or Work Environment

Extensive travel to Rasuwa and Nuwakot of up to 60% of working time. Field travel may involve difficult road conditions, disrupted access, remote locations, and basic accommodation.

Physical Requirements

Willingness and physical ability to travel to Rasuwa and Nuwakot, including remote and disaster-affected locations, for up to 60% of working time.

Language Requirements

Excellent written and spoken English and Nepali, with a demonstrated ability to write reports for donors and external stakeholders.

“World Vision is committed to achieving diversity, as the diversity of our teams is critical to our overall success. WV welcomes applications from qualified professionals all over Nepal. Women, people with disability, and members from other marginalized groups are strongly encouraged to apply.”

“Children and vulnerable adults who come into contact with WV as a result of our activities must be safeguarded to the maximum possible extent from deliberate or inadvertent actions and failings that place them at risk of abuse, sexual exploitation, injury, and any other harm. One of the ways that WVI Nepal shows this on-going commitment to safeguarding is to include rigorous background and reference checks in the selection process for all candidates, in accordance to its Child and Adult Safeguarding Policy. WVI Nepal has zero tolerance to child rights’ violations, by employees and/or affiliates.”

WVI Nepal reserves all rights to qualify/disqualify applications in any case.

Duty Station: Kathmandu with extensive travel to project sites in Rasuwa

Report to: Head of Programme Development

The Project Manager is overall responsible to lead the effective, timely, accountable, and policy-compliant implementation of the REGAIN project in coordination with government, non-government, and community stakeholders.

2. Roles and responsibilities

2.1 Policy, Compliance and Governance

  • Adhere to relevant policies, procedures, regulations and guidelines of HELVETAS Swiss Intercooperation (Code of Conduct; NPR-Nepal; Finance Manual; Security Response Guide; Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Guide; Mobbing, Sexual Harassment & Abuse of Authority; Code of Conduct Against Corruption etc.) and other specific policies applicable for the project;
  • Ensure Conflict Sensitive Programme Management at all levels;
  • Ensure compliance of all the terms and conditions agreed between HELVETAS Swiss Intercooperation Nepal and the donor.

2.2 Project Leadership and Management

  • Provide strategic leadership and overall responsibility for project delivery, results, and performance.
  • Lead annual planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, documentation, and reporting of project and the sub-projects
  • Develop and oversee operational systems and provide technical support to staff and partners.
  • Organize review, planning, learning, and stakeholder engagement events.
  • Conduct field monitoring, assess progress, adapt strategies, commission studies, and ensure quality outputs.
  • Ensure effective M&E systems, timely evaluations, knowledge management, and donor-quality reporting.

2.3 Finance and Administration

  • Oversee project finance and administration in line with HELVETAS and donor requirements.
  • Prepare, review, and revise project budgets; monitor expenditures and ensure financial control.
  • Facilitate internal and external audits.

2.4 Coordination, Representation and Partnerships

  • Ensure effective local coordination through field staff.
  • Maintain good relationship with project staff, partner’s team and related stakeholders to contribute in achieving the goals and objectives of the project.
  • Represent the project in relevant forums, workshops, meetings, and networks.
  • Contribute to HELVETAS country programme management processes.

2.5 People Management and Capacity Development

  • Assess staff development needs, provide coaching and mentoring, and strengthen partner capacities.
  • Plan and implement capacity-building initiatives linked to project objectives.

2.6 Additional Responsibilities

  • Promote innovation, continuous improvement, and new programme initiatives.

Minimum 7 years of experience in humanitarian response, disaster management, emergency relief, or early recovery, including at least 3 years in senior project management roles. Experience managing projects, human resources, finance, administration, and partners. Experience working with government agencies in post-disaster contexts.

In addition, the Finance and Administrative Manager shall also be responsible for supporting and monitoring the partners for proper financial management of the project. S/he shall act as the human resources focal person of the project.

2. Roles and Responsibilities:

2.1 Compliance to policies, rules/regulations and guidelines

  • Adhere to relevant policies, procedures, regulations and guidelines of HELVETAS Swiss Intercooperation (Code of Conduct; NPR-Nepal; Finance Manual; Security Response Guide; Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Guide; Mobbing, Sexual Harassment & Abuse of Authority; Code of Conduct Against Corruption etc.) and other specific policies applicable for the Project;
  • Ensure Conflict Sensitive Programme Management at all levels;
  •  Manage the Human Resource Information System of the project;
  • Ensure compliance of all the terms and conditions agreed between HELVETAS Swiss Intercooperation Nepal and the donor.

2.2 Planning, Budgeting, Monitoring and Reporting

  •  Support Project Manager in preparation of annual budget, Yearly Plan of Operation (YPO), financial report and periodic project financial reports;
  • Financial forecasting, budgeting, monitoring and supervision of the overall financial system;
  •  Reporting of Budget vs. Actual financial report on monthly basis to the Project Manager;
  •  Consolidate and analyse various finance related data to support planning, management and reporting;
  •  Ensure an effective internal control system (ICS);
  •  Receive and keep track of the Programme audit reports and follow up on the audit remarks;
  •  Develop financial discipline within the project.

2.3 Financial Management

  • Countersign and approve vouchers / expenses with Project Manager;
  • Ensure Salary/benefits, allowances, and financial advance management of all project staff;
  • Maintain up to date accounts of all transactions by the project, with adherence to Financial policy, Nepal Accounting Standard (NAS), and International Accounting Standard (IAS), in a transparent manner;
  •  Manage project’s bank accounts; Countersign cheques;
  • Prepare and update bank reconciliation statements on a monthly basis;
  • Proper Management of Income Tax and Value Added Tax (VAT), including reclaiming VAT on a regular basis;
  • Proper management of payments (i.e., Contractors, suppliers, salary payment to staffs, consultants, and any others, as per established financial rules and regulations;
  • Ensure the transparent and competitive procurement of goods and services at all times;
  • Development of various financial forms as required;
  • Advise procurement committee on issues of finance as requested;
  • Financial closing and management of accounts;
  • Prepare financial plans and periodic financial statement.
  • Ensure timely and proper records of all financial transactions.
  • Ensure timely and accurate financial reporting as per the organizational and donor’s requirement.
  • Capacitate finance team of the project and assist in the capacity building of and leading partner companies in developing their capacity in accounting and financial management.

2.4 Administrative and Human Resources management

  •  Liaison with the project staff to ensure that they are aware of all of the administrative systems and procedures;
  •  Lead international and local procurement (where tenders/quotations are required) as a procurement focal person for the project in accordance with HELVETAS Nepal procurement procedures of goods and services;
  •  Advising the project team on procurement, awarding of contracts and payment procedures, and supplying the required information, s/he shall be a permanent member of the procurement committee;
  •  Office management and day-to-day administration of the Project.
  •  Ensure efficient vehicle and logistics management and support;
  •  Preparation of contractors’, consultants’ agreements, and contracts, in accordance with programme rules and regulations and available budget;
  • •Management of insurance for the project staff including, liaison with insurance companies to process claims;
  • Effective and efficient inventory management;
  • Act as a HR focal person of the project
  •  Coordinate and facilitate for the recruitment process of the project as necessary;
  • Ensure proper induction to new employees on orgainisational policies and guidelines;
  • Contribute for a fair, inclusive, and equitable working environment within the project;
  •  Plan and implement capacity building activities for project and partner staff members;
  •  Ensure proper documentation and confidential of personal records and other HR documents of project staff;
  •  Manage the Human Resource Information System of the project.

2.5 Others

  • Other tasks as and when necessary and as requested by the Project Manager.

3. Job Requirements

3.1 Minimum Education and Professional Experience:

  • Master’s degree in Business Administration, Management, or Commerce with Finance/Accounting as a major subject, or a professional accountancy degree. Minimum 5 years of work experience managing overall finance and accounting of the project, preferably in an international organization.

3.2 Required competencies:

  • Strong ability in supervision of overall financial systems with inclusive frameworks and procedures
  •  Good understanding of national rules and regulations
  •  Understanding of development programme budgeting and financial monitoring
  •  Good understanding of VAT/ Tax rules and regulations
  •  Good time management and task prioritization skills
  •  Commitment towards gender equality, social inclusion, and poverty reduction
  •  Result-oriented maintaining deadlines
  •  Excellent interpersonal, intercultural competencies and team player
  •  Ability to work independently with a minimum level of supervision
  •  Showing initiative in making processes more effective and cost efficient
  • Fluency in Nepali and English, both written and oral
  • Proficiency in using office application software, especially good working knowledge of MS-Excel

Additional Information

Any telephone enquiries/and or attempts to apply undue influence will result disqualification of candidates. Only short-listed candidates will be contacted for the selection process. Helvetas Nepal reserves the right to reject any or all applications without assigning any reasons.

Helvetas Nepal promotes workforce diversity and applies positive discrimination to candidates from discriminated groups (Women, Dalit, Janajati, Madhesi/Terai, and other minority communities).
